articleTitle: Polarization profiling of the surface region of PVDF and P(VDF-TrFE)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Inhomogeneous polarization profiles are a typical property of ferroelectric polymers. Particularly in the surface region, the occurrence of a nonpolar layer is often observed. Different mechanisms can cause the decrease of the polarization near the surface. The first is the injection of charge from the metal contacts into the polymer during the poling when high electric fields are applied to the sample. The second is a structural variation of the sample near the surface e. g., a lower degree of crystallinity than in the bulk. The LIMM method i.e., a scan of the polarization profile with thermal waves, is particularly appropriate for an investigation of the surface near region of a sample. The resolution of LIMM has been improved to be better than 100 nm by an increase of the modulation frequencies into the MHz region. With this increased resolution, the surface near polarization in samples of polyvinylidenefluoride and its copolymers with trifluorethylene has been investigated.

articleTitle: Space charge measurement by the Thermal Step method and TSDC in PMMA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The Thermal Step method elaborated by A. Toureille at the Laboratoire d'Electrotechnique de Montpellier is based on the measurement of thermodilatation current due to the application of a thermal step, to one side of the sample. The deconvolution of this current gives the repartition of electrical field and space charges inside the insulator. This method has been used for the first time to study repartition of polarization and space charge in polar material such as PMMA (polymethyl-methacrylate). Coupling this technique with Thermally Stimulated Discharge Current method (TSDC), it is possible to see minority carriers which could be masked by majority carriers. It allowed us to reveal injection, which was not visible when only the thermal step method was used, because it was masked by important polarization.

articleTitle: Properties of PP-PS double layer electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A simplified analysis of the double layer electret with a frozen space charge leads to a conclusion that such a structure can show a piezo-effect in case of difference in elasticity coefficients of both layers. Results of the experiments carried out on the PP-PS foil electrets confirmed that the value of piezoelectric coefficient can be comparable to that of PVDF films. Investigation of the TSD current has shown that the charge storage properties of the structure are mainly determined by the properties of the PP layer.

articleTitle: Improved silicon dioxide electret for silicon-based integrated microphones
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Capacitor microphones integrated on silicon chips are being designed to operate at lower bias voltage but still require either a voltage multiplier circuit or an electret. Conventional electret materials are difficult to process with silicon and their processing temperature limitations results in their unpopularity in the fabrication of silicon integrated microphones. Attempts to use electrets of silicon dioxide and silicon nitride have not been successful due to poor charge stability. A better technique was found by overcoating the silicon dioxide with dielectrics. This paper will describe films of silicon dioxide overcoated with tantalum pentoxide using sputtering and electron-beam deposition. The charge retention characteristic of tantalum pentoxide are highly dependent on forming conditions. Hence, the processing conditions and various annealing methods will be described and related to charge stability. Variations in charge density and distribution on exposure to elevated temperature and humidity will be reported.

articleTitle: Dielectric nonlinearities of P(VDF-TrFE)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The nonlinear dielectric permittivities of copolymers of polyvinylidenfluoride (PVDF) with trifluoroethylene (TrFE) have been measured as a function of temperature. The phase transition from the ferroelectric to the paraelectric phase is characterised by the sign of the third order permittivity in the paraelectric phase. The observed third order permittivity is positive for a copolymer of 70/30 mol% VDF-TrFE, but negative for 56/44 mol-% VDF-TrFE. This shows a change of the nature of the phase transition with the composition. Poling of the material causes a strong increase of the permittivities of even order in the ferroelectric phase, while the linear dielectric constant and the odd order permittivities slightly decrease. In the paraelectric phase, the investigated 56/44 mol-% VDF-TrFE specimens show a non vanishing second order permittivity. This deviation of the inversion symmetry is described by an internal bias field. While the absolute value of the bias field varies for different samples, it is found to be independent of temperature and a previous poling.

articleTitle: Space charge distributions in insulating polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Recently, new non-destructive techniques such as the LIPP, PIPS, PEA and TP methods have been developed to measure directly the space charge distributions in solid dielectrics. These techniques are very powerful to understand the space charge in insulating materials. In this paper, these new techniques have been briefly reviewed. The space charge distributions and behaviors in insulating polymers, especially in polyethylene, have been shown. The space charge effects on the high-field conduction and breakdown phenomena in polyethylene have been also discussed quantitatively.

articleTitle: Miniaturized inorganic electret layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Silicon dioxide and nitride based materials are interesting inorganic electrets for applications in the field of micromechanics and sensor technologies since they are compatible to the silicon technology. It was the motivation for this work to find new suitable electret materials with good mechanical properties for the application in a micromachined electret condenser microphone. SiO/sub 2/, Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ single and double layers and SiON layers are investigated in terms of chargeability and long-term charge-stability. The main emphasis is put on the miniaturization of electret layers. The lateral dimensions of the electrets are reduced down to 2 mm and the characteristics under different environmental conditions are described.

articleTitle: Direct evaluation of thermal-pulse, thermal-step, and thermal-wave results for obtaining charge and polarization profiles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The most difficult problem with the thermal techniques for the investigation of charge and polarization profiles in electrets is the signal interpretation. Because of the diffusive character of heat transport, the useful information is distributed on a /spl radic/t scale for the thermal-pulse and thermal-step techniques and on a /spl radic//spl omega/ scale for the thermal-wave technique. The resolution of the techniques is high near the heated surface and becomes smaller inside the film. It is shown that properly scaled, measured signals already represent a good estimate of the electric-field or polarization distribution. Experimental results from thermal-pulse investigations of 25 /spl mu/m thick electron-beam charged Teflon films, and of nominally well poled 25 /spl mu/m thick PVDF films as well as thermal-wave investigations of a 1.3 /spl mu/m thick double-layer of nonlinear optical (NLO) polymers with two different glass-transition temperatures demonstrate the strengths of the concept.

articleTitle: Thermal wave methods: some experimental pitfalls
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Uncertainties in the spatial distributions calculated from thermal wave data are normally attributed to the ill-posed deconvolution problem. This paper focusses on the impact of "ill-posed" experimental conditions on the pyroelectric spectra. The spectra are affected by structural inhomogeneities and temporal changes in the electrical and thermal properties, by distortions caused by the electric circuit, by frequency-dependent properties and by piezoelectricity. Experimental results are given for PVDF and LiTaO/sub 3/. Suggestions are made to reduce the effect of experimental errors.

articleTitle: Effect of the thickness of insulators on the build up of a space charge distribution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: When an electric stress is applied to an insulator, a space charge distribution may develop and have a strong effect on the electric strength of the material. It has already been reported that the thickness of the insulator may have an effect on the observed phenomena. In this paper we have investigated this effect, using the pressure wave propagation (PWP) method, and present experimental results which have been obtained on pure polyethylene samples of different thicknesses with similar electrodes, submitted to the same applied electric field. These results show that the distribution of space charge depends on the thickness for a given material, but not the maximum value of the charge density. The effect of dopant is also considered by comparison with already reported data.

articleTitle: Old and new poling techniques for nonlinear optical polymer electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Polymers with second-order optical nonlinearities contain molecular dipoles as guest molecules, side groups, or main-chain segments. Macroscopic nonlinear optical effects including the electro-optical effect are obtained only after preferential orientation of the dipoles by means of poling. At least in principle, the full range of known electret poling techniques can be employed with nonlinear optical polymer electrets. In addition, a few new poling methods were developed specifically for them. Since relatively high glass-transition temperatures are required for stable amorphous nonlinear optical polymers, poling must usually be performed at elevated temperatures. In addition to the often used classical electrode and corona poling techniques, electron-beam poling was recently proposed for selective poling of nonlinear optical polymers. Furthermore, new poling methods such as photothermal poling with local heating by a light beam and photo-induced poling exploiting the photo-isomerism of molecular dipoles are being introduced. These poling techniques will be discussed and compared, and the possible use of the newly developed methods on other electrets will be considered.

articleTitle: Binding energies of trapped charges in PVDF and P(VDF/TrFE)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The remanent polarization in PVDF and P(VDF/TrFE) is stabilized by trapped charges. We measured the remanent polarization P as function of temperature during heating from room temperature to 180/spl deg/C. The discharge current is then computed as the first derivative -dP/dT. Assuming a Debye relaxation and a continuous distribution of binding energies g(E) of the trapped charges we can show that the discharge current I(T) is proportional to g(E=mT), with m=const. The constant m can either be calculated numerically or by analytical approximation, With this method the distribution g(E) can be determined. These data are consistent with the extraordinary long life time of the remanent polarisation in PVDF and P(VDF/TrFE) at room temperature.

articleTitle: Application of electrets in traumatology and orthopedy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A positive influence of electro-stimulation upon the regeneration of an injured osseous tissue is known. In the work presented, we solve the problem of increasing the efficacy of treating bone/joint injuries and disease using electrets based on films of anodic tantalum oxide, polytetrafluoroethylene and its copolymers, these thin layers covering the surface of complicate-formed fixators of bone fragments. The results are given of investigating electret properties of the said films, depending on methods of obtaining electrization, stabilization and operation. It is shown that the stability, if the films' electret state is obtained under optimum conditions, is sufficient for prolonged and efficacious stimulation of an osteoreparation process in the electroconductive and aggressive environment within the organism.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of the electret state and the interfacial origin of piezoelectricity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Beginning with the Gibbs' thermodynamic equation for electrocapillary action at a charged interface between two phases, it is possible to derive an interfacial model for piezoelectricity. This model is applied to the situation in a poled material like PVDF where the synergistic interaction between polarization in the crystallite phases and trapped charge in the amorphous phases leads to a system of charged interfaces which not only stabilize the polarization but also become the sources of piezoelectricity.

articleTitle: PP-based blends for electret filters-an appraisal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Corona-charged polypropylene-based polymeric materials for electret filters were studied. Blending of PP with polycarbonate was found not to improve its performance, despite claims made elsewhere. The electret properties were characterized with several techniques, including one that allows the determination of the fine structure of all trap-depth energies. Trapping near the crystallites provides most of the deep traps in PP-based polymers. A more perfect crystallite structure thus enhances the charge stability. This fact offers better opportunities for producing longlasting electret filters than blending with PC. A crucial factor is that the PP-blend should remain nonpolar in order to guarantee a low conductivity and high water repellency.

articleTitle: Piezopolymer transducers in the active control of vibrations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: This paper presents the active vibration control of rectangular thin plates by PVDF piezopolymer transducers. Theoretical and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Behaviour of /spl rho/ relaxation in polarization cyclic processes by TSDC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: It has been studied the p relaxation reproductibility of TSDC discharges obtained from PET-a and PMMA electrets formed by windowing polarization. It has been observed that this relaxation is sensitive to the sample initial conditions. Cyclic charge-discharge treatments, carried out on these samples keeping all the polarization parameters constant, results in a trapping capability increase which seems to have a purely electrical origin and it also seems to be sensitive to electrical ageing.

articleTitle: Enhancement of piezoelectric activity in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer using two-step poling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The piezoelectric property of thick P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer films could be enhanced by a two-step thermal poling method. Two weak resonance peaks were observed after the first poling, while only a single strong resonance was found after the two-step poling process. To study the mechanisms of the polarization process, X-ray diffraction (XRD) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) were used. The results were reported.

articleTitle: A chronological review of production and applications of electret condenser microphone for consumer use
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Mass production of electret condenser microphones (ECM) built into compact cassette tape recorders for consumer use started in 1970. The key issues were the FEP electret foil and the integrated circuit including FET and resistor. The production grew according to progress of applications which was widened to stereo equipments and to communication equipments. Materials and fabricating technologies have coped with the demands due to increasing quantity and diversifying requirements. The microphones have changed to smaller size and directional characteristics. The present dominant requirement is for higher temperature specifications for automated assembly systems.

articleTitle: Charge trapping sites in spherulitic polypropylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Charged areas of positively corona-charged spherulitic polypropylene films were visualized with photoionized dye vapor. From visualized charge patterns, location for charge trapping sites for a low temperature TSC bands B/sub L/ and a high temperature band B/sub H/, which are observed above room temperature in spherulitic polypropylene were determined: traps for B/sub L/ and B/sub H/ exist mainly in the peripheral and central parts of spherulites, respectively.

articleTitle: A dielectric study of poly-ether-ether-ketone (PEEK) and poly-ether-sulphone (PES) films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Many polymers such as Teflon and the polyolefines can be used to produce electrets which have a relatively stable external electrical field as a result of ordered molecular dipoles or the presence of stable charges. The dielectric behaviour of such materials under the influence of electrical fields is important for the formation of electrets. The relatively new aromatic polymers of poly(ether sulphone), PES, and poly(ether ether ketone), PEEK, are important engineering materials due to their good electrical and mechanical properties. However little data is available on their dielectric behaviour which is important in the evaluation of their potential use as materials for electrets. In this study dielectric behaviour of PES and PEEK was examined over a range of temperatures and electric field strengths by employing the techniques of isothermal transient current measurement (TC) and thermally stimulated discharging current measurement (TSDC). Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was also undertaken to establish any correlation between structural changes and dielectric behaviour.

articleTitle: Micromachined silicon subminiature microphones with piezoelectric P(VDF/TRFE)-layers and silicon-nitride-membranes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper a silicon subminiature microphone is described, which is based on the piezoelectric effect of spin-coated P(VDF/TrFE)-layers. The polymer layers are placed on top of a very thin silicon nitride membrane, which is implanted with boron ions in order to reduce the tensile stress of the diaphragm, resulting in higher microphone sensitivities. A maximum sensitivity of 150 /spl mu/V/Pa, a bandwidth of about 16 kHz and an equivalent noise level of less than 60 dB(A) were measured. Considering the small area of the membrane of the microphone (1 mm/sup 2/), the sensors show a much better performance than former microphones with piezoelectric polymer layers.

articleTitle: Influence of environment humidity on properties of FEP, PTFE, PCTFE and PI film electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of environmental humidity on charge storage stability was investigated by means of isothermal surface potential decay and open-circuit TSD measurement. The shift of mean charge depth for these materials at different environmental humidities was studied by using the heat pulse technique.

articleTitle: Comparison of charge distributions in FEP measured with thermal wave and pressure pulse techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The spatial distribution of charges, injected by monoenergetic electrons in Teflon FEP have been determined by two different techniques, i.e. laser-induced pressure pulse (LIPP) technique, and laser-intensity modulation method (LIMM). A comparison of the results, provided by the two techniques shows good agreement.

articleTitle: Thermal pulse measurements on electron-beam irradiated fluoroethylene-propylene copolymer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The electric charge distribution in the fluoroethylene-propylene copolymer (FEP or FEP-Teflon) Induced by a partially penetrating electron beam has been probed using the thermal pulse (TP) method. Deconvolution of TP transients clearly indicate that negative charge has accumulated at a mean depth dependent on the energy of the electrons in the beam. Good agreement between measured and computer-generated TP transients is obtained by using model distributions with positive near-surface charge layers in addition to the negative implanted charge layer.

articleTitle: New applications of electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Applications of electrets are discussed which were either newly realized over the past few years or which represent significantly improved implementations of older devices. Among these applications are optical polymer waveguides, solar cells, radiation dosimeters, silicon microphones, air-sampling systems, pyroelectric arrays, and piezoelectric transducers. Brief descriptions of these devices are supplemented by references to the literature.

articleTitle: Electric polarization induced by strain gradient
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Electric polarization induced by a strain gradient-flexoelectricity-is studied theoretically on the system of parallel chains of harmonic oscillators. Instead of the strain gradient, the external forces are chosen as an external parameter. They are applied on the boundary of a sample the shape of which ensures nonhomogeneous deformation to be created.

articleTitle: The deconvolution of the fundamental equation of LIMM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: For the deconvolution of LIMM (Laser Intensity Modulation Method) spectra a regularization algorithm based on the self-consistency method developed by Honerkamp and Weese is applied. Linear grids and the one-side irradiated case were considered. We show the simultaneous determination of all important thermal parameters with the spatial distribution. The natural line width (NLW) is determined for our algorithm.

articleTitle: Electret relay matrices for premises information distribution systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper we present a new application of electret relays in the field of matrix switching devices. It should offer a new efficient way to solve the problem of configuring networks in future intelligent buildings.

articleTitle: Thermal stability of the dipole orientation in nonlinear optical guest-host, side-chain and cross-linked polymer electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: As the thermal stability of nonlinear optical polymer electrets is essential for their application in waveguide devices, three typical polymers were studied by means of isothermal pyroelectricity measurements and thermally stimulated depolarization experiments. The fundamental difference between the three sample materials is the connection between the polymer backbone and the nonlinear optical molecules: The guest-host polymer is just doped with chromophore molecules, in the side-chain material, the chromophore is chemically linked to the main-chain, and in the cross-linked system, chromophore movement is still further restricted. The numerical evaluation reveals how the isothermal relaxation deviates from an exponential decay, and the TSD results yield the product of activation energy and stretching parameter. The behavior of guest-host and side-chain polymers can be described by a single broad relaxation process, whereas cross-linking yields a rigid dipole polymer network with a high activation temperature of the dipole orientation.

articleTitle: LIMM investigations of thermally poled PVDF and FEP samples
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The laser intensity modulation method (LIMM) was applied to the investigation of polarization and/or space charge distributions in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and Teflon FEP. The poling procedure was carried out in a small temperature window, /spl Delta/T=5 K, and the poling parameters electric field E/sub p/ and time t/sub p/ were varied. In the deconvolution of the LIMM spectra we introduce a new promising spatial grid distribution. For PVDF we have found results in accordance with literature data, the so-called "thermal profile" (near the anode-side). The FEP sample have shown an electric field distribution, which is concentrated near the anode as well as the cathode-side. Therefore, the space charge distribution is located in the middle region of the sample.

articleTitle: Silicon based electret relays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper we present a new family of integrated electret relays, the various parts of them being made by micromachining of silicon wafers. Ageing curves of electrets which are directly made on the silicon substrates will be shown, and new mechanical designs will be described.

articleTitle: Correlation between space charge distributions and external current measurements during the discharge of low density polyethylene samples
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A new experimental set-up which allows simultaneous measurements of both charge profiles by the pressure wave propagation (PWP) method and total external current has been developed. It has been applied to the study of low density polyethylene. The displacement current can be determined everywhere in the sample. During the discharge, the external current and displacement current are shown to be very similar at both electrodes. A good agreement is obtained between the zero-field plane current model and the measured external current.

articleTitle: Cold plasma-deposited SiO/sub 2/ and amorphous Teflon AF as electret-coatings for MIS-IL solar cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Novel thin film materials, namely cold plasma-deposited SiO/sub 2/ and spin-coated Teflon AF have recently been identified as useful electrets; the present paper briefly summarises preparation conditions and material characteristics, the main attention being focused on the applicability of these electrets to MIS-solar cells (Metal Insulator Semiconductor). As a functional coating, the electret passivates the surface and generates a permanent electric field which induces an inversion zone at the silicon surface between the metal lines of the front electrode. It is shown that the I-V-characteristic drastically depends on the polarity and density of the electret space charge. Hence, electrets in solar cell technology can be an important means to increase the device efficiency, and to study silicon-insulator interfaces.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated currents in natural diamonds
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The results of thermally stimulated depolarization currents in natural Yakut diamonds are presented. In the temperature range 200-650 K two peaks of TSD currents are observed; a low-temperature peak at 325 K and a high-temperature peak at 540 K. Repeated thermal cycling in the above temperature range leads to transformation of TSD current curves: the value of the high-temperature peak decreases and the value of the low temperature peak increases. The calculation of parameters of electrically active defects responsible for observed TSD current peaks gives the following values: W/sub lt/=0.68 eV, /spl omega//sub lt/=5 10/sup 8/ s/sup -1/; W/sub ht/=18 eV, /spl omega//sub ht/=5 10/sup 8/ s/sup -1/.

articleTitle: New results concerning thermally stimulated discharge current peak above room temperature
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally Stimulated Discharge Current measurements an as received polarized and electron-beam charged samples as well as DC conductivity and isothermal current measurements were used in the attempt of understanding the nature of peaks above room temperature in poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) samples. The mechanism by which the external measured current is produced is analyzed and a new model is proposed. In this model the polarization charge and the injected charge give an heterocharge type current in very accord with experimental results. The homocharge type peaks results from adsorbed ions and only when the measurements are made at pressure higher than 5*10/sup -2/ torr. The maximum above T/sub g/ is determined by the space-charge movement by hopping mechanisms. The stored charge comportment at high temperature can be studied by the new proposed measuring methods: Thermally Stimulated Space Charge (TSSC) and isothermal final discharging current measurement. The importance of external measuring resistance is analyzed.

articleTitle: Amorphous covalent dielectrics-new category of materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The concept of amorphous covalent dielectrics is presented. It is shown that plasma-deposited Si-C and Ge-C films exist in two qualitatively different groups. The first group consists of typical amorphous semiconductors while the second one is categorized as amorphous dielectrics. The most important feature distinguishing one group from another is the lack of extended states in the dielectrics.

articleTitle: The piezoelectric properties of organic piezoelectric crystals p-phenyl-thiourea
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: This paper illustrates significance of a new type organic electronic crystal based on substituted phenyl-thiourea. The synthesis preparation, molecular structure, dielectric and piezoelectric properties, analysis etc. are discussed.

articleTitle: Material anisotropy effects on space charge distribution in high voltage cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: High voltage XLPE (Cross-Linked PolyEthylene) insulated cables can reveal some angular anisotropy of material properties due to extrusion and characterised by a higher level of residual stresses. These stressed regions are located by birefringence measurements and found at precise and reproducible location in the dielectric. This parameter has been taken into account since the beginning of this work. The cable under investigation was electrically aged in laboratory at a maximum AC field of 27 kV/mm for 3000 hours. The influence of both the level of residual stresses and high field electrical ageing on the physico-chemical and dielectric properties of the XLPE has been studied. The space charge distribution in the insulating wall, induced by application of a DC polarisation, has been measured using the Pressure Wave Propagation method (PWP) at different angular locations in the cable. The anisotropy of material properties is revealed by this method. This work also shows that the angular parameter must be integrated for any study on cable material ageing.

articleTitle: Charge distributions in electron-beam irradiated Kapton PI and Teflon FEP films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Charge distributions in 25 /spl mu/m thick films of Kapton PI and Teflon FEP, charged with 20 and 30 keV electron beams, are measured with the laser-induced pressure-pulse (LIPP) method directly after charging or after additional annealing periods at 120/spl deg/C. The charge distributions show changes with annealing time which suggest slow and fast retrapping, with Schubwegs at 120/spl deg/C of >20 /spl mu/m and /spl sim/5 /spl mu/m for PI and FEP, respectively. Corresponding /spl mu//spl tau/-products are >6/spl times/10/sup -9/ and /spl sim/10/sup -9/ cm/sup 2//V.

articleTitle: Determination of charge centroid in thin films by corona-charging and TSD techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A new method to determine the charge centroid in thin films is proposed, based on corona charging and thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) techniques as well as surface potential measurement. The method consists in superimposing the opposite polarity charge and thereafter subjecting the sample to TSD. The surface potential varies with charge detrapping and neutralization. The original charge centroid can be derived from these parameters under the assumption that the activation energies are different for positive and negative carriers and the origin charge has higher activation energy. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results are given.

articleTitle: Electrical investigation of electron-beam poled nonlinear optical polymer electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: An electron-beam method is used for the poling of two nonlinear optical polymers, namely a guest-host material, Disperse Red 1/Poly (methyl methacrylate) and a side-chain polymer based on a styrene-co-maleic-anhydride polymer and Disperse Red 1 chromophore side groups. Details of the poling process are reported together with results from laser-induced pressure-pulse (LIPP) polarization-profile scans. Results of thermally stimulated current (TSC) measurements are also discussed. An evaluation of the experimental data shows that under the present experimental conditions, only the guest-host polymer can be poled while the side-chain polymer shows a space charge but no polarization.

articleTitle: Charge decay and transportation in teflon AF films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Isothermal surface potential decay and thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) are performed with amorphous polymer teflon AF films, which is a new member of the teflon family with a lot of unique features. The experimental results show that the charge retention in this material is quite good as long as the field across the films is not too high. Heat treatment before and after charging changes the TSD peaks and consequently the charge stability for negative charging. In the case of positive charging, a more significant effect occurs when the sample is charged at elevated temperatures.

articleTitle: T.S.C. study of liquid-liquid transition in polyvinyl chloride
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The thermally stimulated current (T.S.C.) diagrams have been recorded above 0/spl deg/C, with samples obtained by pelleting under a pressure of 3.5 T/cm/sup 2/, the PVC powder. These T.S.C diagrams, obtained with conditions of polarization T/sub p/=125/spl deg/C, tp=2 min., F/sub p/=3.10/sup 5/ V/m, have shown at 80/spl deg/C. In the neighbourhood of the glass transition, a first peak with a shoulder towards 55/spl deg/C. A second peak, associated to a liquid-liquid transition appears at 123/spl deg/C. The ratio T/sub ll/(/spl deg/K)/Tg(/spl deg/K)=1.13 is close to those obtained with different polymers by different authors. The T/sub ll/ follows a Vogel-W.L.F. law /spl tau/=/spl tau//sub 0/exp(/spl alpha//sub r/(T-/spl infin/))/sup -1/ where T/sub /spl infin//=304/spl deg/K.

articleTitle: Space charge due to contact effects in Al-polyethylene terephthalate-Al systems: modeling and study by the thermally stimulated current method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The Thermally Stimulated Depolarization Current method allowed us to emphasize the role played by aluminum-polyester contacts on the electrical properties of Metal-Polyethylene Terephthalate films-Metal systems. Assuming the existence of Schottky barriers at the Al-PET interfaces after heat treatment, the electronic band model permitted us to account for the nature and properties of the space charge in annealed PET films (1.5 to 12 /spl mu/m), in a wide range of poling temperatures, times and fields.

articleTitle: The percolation behaviour of electret at presence of water condensation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The time stability of the surface potential of PTFE and silicon dioxide electrets at room temperature are similar: after an initial small decay the potential is practically constant during a time interval that decreases as humidity increases and then drastically drops. The time stability of the surface is correlated with potential relief of an electret sample. The presence of charge on a dielectric surface stimulates the process of water condensation. The behavior of electrets in a wet atmosphere is explained in terms of the percolation model that includes the process of nucleation and growth of conductive clusters. A theoretical consideration within a framework of this model and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Water induced TSDC in hemoglobin and myoglobin
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The hydration of hemoglobin (Hb) and myoglobin (Mb) has been investigated by the Thermally Stimulated Depolarization Currents (TSDC) technique. The TSDC spectra as a function of the hydration degree (/spl delta/=0.01+0.3 grams of water/grams of protein) and of the annealing time in vacuum were recorded in the temperature range 100-300 K on pellet samples. The distribution of water dipoles for both heme-proteins shows four main peaks in the range 170-300 K, indicating the presence of at least four different classes of bound water. A fifth peak at very low temperatures (T/sub m//spl sim/150 K) appears only at low hydration levels and probably it is not related to water dipole relaxations. Possible environments of water dipoles responsible for the TSDC peaks are discussed.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated electric changes during the helix to coil transition of irradiated DNA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The purpose of the present work was to investigate early changes evolved in the DNA macromolecule during its helix to coil phase transition following exposure to ionizing radiation. This phase transition measures the thermostability of this macromolecule and it is greatly affected by exposure to ionizing radiations apparently due to induced single strand and double strand breaks on either or the two coils of the double DNA helix. Our results indicate that conductivity changes definitely preceding the helix to coil transition. This observation is on line with the suggested precedence of hydrophobic bonds disruption prior to hydrogen bonds disruption which coincides with this type of phase transition that finally leads to the denaturation of the DNA.

articleTitle: Dielectric hysteresis in some polyamides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In view of the electric displacement D-the electric field E hysteresis or the polarization reversal in less crystalline polyamides derived from m-xylylenediamine we have investigated the ferroelectric nature in other types of polyamide. In this work samples employed were polyamides prepared from 1,3-bis(aminomethyl)cyclohexane (BAC) and dicarboxylic acids with the number of carbon atoms n=6,7, and 10 and from hexamethylenediamine (HMD) and isophthalic acid(I), and from HMD and 70 mol% I and 30 mol% terephthalic acid(T) which were abbreviated to nylon BAC n, nylon 6I (6, the number of carbon atoms in HMD), and nylon 6I/6T, respectively. Nylon BAC 6,7, and 10 showed the glass transition at 376, 362, and 346K, respectively, as observed by the differential thermal analysis (DTA) method. Quenched samples of nylon BAC exhibited the D-E hysteresis irrespective of the number of carbon atom, of which the remanent polarization P/sub I/ and the coercive field E/sub c/ were about 30 mC m/sup -2/ and 80 MV m/sup -1/, respectively. Nylon 6I and 6I/6T were amorphous, showing neither crystallization nor fusion temperature in the DTA thermogram, and exhibiting the D-E hysteresis with the same order of magnitude of P/sub r/ and E/sub c/ as those in nylon BAC n at high temperature near 370K. The remanent polarization in poled polyamides studied was depolarized near the glass transition with increasing temperature. The polarization of the amide groups in amorphous regions was considered to be responsible for the dielectric hysteresis in these polyamides.

articleTitle: Piezo- and pyroelectric properties of dehydrofluorinated PVDF films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: PVDF was effectively dehydrofluorinated by the reaction with hot alkali-DMSO solution. PVDF degrades to products containing c=c, c=c, and c=0 groups as revealed by the corresponding bands in the IR spectrum. Because of the formation of conjugated c=c double bonds in the polymer chain, films of degraded PVDF become darker. Films have been produced by casting onto a glass plate. These cast films were stretched and poled. The results of the measurements of the piezoelectric strain coefficient d/sub 31/ and of the pyroelectric coefficient p/sub 3/ are given in comparison with undegraded films. Moderately pyroelectric coefficients of dehydrofluorinated PVDF films and their enhanced absorbance makes them attractive for potential applications in fast pyroelectric sensors.

articleTitle: The isothermal discharge of a polystyrene electret via a distribution of electron trapping states
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The distribution in energy of trapping states in a polymer may be studied by populating the traps and observing the current that accompanies the relaxation of the trapped charges. In this relaxation process the carriers from shallow traps are thermally excited, move a short distance, and become retrapped in deeper lying states, and so on through a multiple trapping scheme. The states may be populated by injection from an electron beam. The isothermal discharge that follows the initial charging event takes on a particularly simple form in the non-retrapping limit. The general case of arbitrary distribution of states with retrapping can be analyzed by using a multiple trapping formalism, and this analysis yields the required distribution of trapping states in the dielectric. We use this multiple trapping analysis solution to examine the shortcoming of the non-trapping, approximate solution to the isothermal discharge.

articleTitle: On the nature of homocharge accumulation and polarization phenomena in thin polymeric layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: It was established that inhomogeneity in conductivity between the regions near the surfaces and the bulk of thin polymeric layers determine the conformity to natural laws of homocharge accumulation and polarization phenomena in these polymeric layers.

articleTitle: Effects of rare earth doping on the piezo and pyroelectric properties of lead zirconate titanate (PZT)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this study we report the piezoelectric, pyroelectric and dielectric properties of rare earth (Eu/sup 3+/, Gd/sup 3+/. Sm/sup 3+/, Yb/sup 3+/, Nb/sup 5+/) modified PZT ceramics. The conventional mixed oxide route was adopted for preparation of the ceramics. Samples sintered in pellet form were corona poled using a voltage of 7 kV/cm at a temperature of 100 to 200/spl deg/C. Measurements of piezoelectric coefficients, pyroelectric coefficients, dielectric constant and loss are reported. Piezoelectric and pyroelectric figures of merit of these ceramics are also reported. The structural studies of these ceramics were also carried out. It is shown that doping of PZT with different rare earths in the right proportions improves their application in piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices.

articleTitle: C-V-testing of electret transducers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A non-destructive method for electret transducers testing is suggested and discussed. The method allows to determine electret-transducers (microphone, telephone, etc.) insert parameters, e.g. electret surface potential air gap width, membrane tension and deflection. The method is based on the insert C-V-characteristic measurements. C-V-testing method can be also used in investigation of electromechanical properties of two roughed surfaces contact, one of the surfaces being dielectric (electret) and allows to optimize the transducer's geometry and surface potential value.

articleTitle: The study of the intrinsic charges in SiO/sub 2/ electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: It is found that there are four kinds of intrinsic charges in the thermally wet grown SiO/sub 2/ electret. They are positive mobile ionic charges, fixed oxide charges, interface trapped charges and oxide trapped space charges. Our experimental results and theoretical analyses point out that these four kinds of charges in the thermally wet grown SiO/sub 2/ electret affect the structure of the energy levels of the SiO/sub 2/, change the trapping and detrapping conditions of the electrons which are injected into SiO/sub 2/ by means of negative corona charging. In this way they influence the stability of the space charges in the electret remarkably.

articleTitle: Waveguide applications of nonlinear optical polymer electrets with three-dimensional patterning of the dipole polarization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Advanced integrated optical devices with poled polymers require various dipole-orientation patterns. Besides parallel and perpendicular orientations with respect to the film plane, periodic poling structures with alternating polarity along the waveguide direction and with step-like profiles across the active-layer thickness are needed. The nondestructive investigation of the various dipole orientation patterns with electro-optical and pyroelectrical microscopes is described. Applications include mode filtering, polarization-independent light modulation, phase-matched as well as quasi-phase-matched collinear and counterpropagating second-harmonic generation.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated discharge current studies in a polymethyl methacrylate polystyrene blend
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermoelectrets were prepared using polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA), polystyrene (PS) and their blend in the 50:50 weight ratio. The TSDC spectra of PMMA shows both dipolar and space charge peaks, while the TSDC spectra of PS shows only the space charge peak. The TSDC spectra of the blend however, shows only one peak which is the space charge peak. It is therefore concluded that the PMMA dipoles in the blends are constrained or their contribution to thermoelectret formation is either insignificant or is masked by the space charge polarization.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated phenomena in vitreous Ge/sub 28.5/Pb/sub 15/S/sub 56.5/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The thermally activated technique including the thermally stimulated conductivity (TSC) and depolarization (TSD) was used to study the peculiarities of the local states energy spectra in photo- and X-ray sensitive chalcogenide vitreous semiconductors of Ge-Pb-S system. The TSC curves of thin Ge-Pb-S films show 4 peaks. The comparative analysis and direct combination of TSC and TSD methods enlarges their informativity and allows to define the set of local states parameters.

articleTitle: TSC properties of epoxy composites cured with acid-anhydride
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The TSC spectroscopy was applied to investigate an influence of structural change and interfacial state on the electrical properties of epoxy composites cured with acid-anhydride. A addition of over abundant hardener and inorganic filler separated a /spl beta/ peak near 10[/spl deg/C] into two peaks of /spl beta//sub 1/(10/spl deg/C) and /spl beta//sub 2/(20/spl deg/C) and increased magnitude of TSC spectra between /spl alpha/ and /spl beta/ peak, which would be closely related with the process of thermal oxidation and separation of hardener's phenyl group according to an introduction of interfacial deformation, an expansion of free volume and a reduction of structural packing density. And the treatment of silane coupling agents on filler improved interfacial deformation to decrease the amplitude of TSC spectra.

articleTitle: Electro-active properties of intelligent ferroelectric ceramic/polymer composite sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The results of a study of the dielectric, piezo- and pyroelectric properties of calcium modified lead titanate (PTCa), and its composites with (i) copolymer vinylidene fluoride-Trifluoroethylene (VDF-TrFE) and (ii) Epoxy (Epikote 828) are reported. The latter composite, i.e. PTCa/Epikote 828 with 60% vol% ceramic loading appear to have superior properties for piezoelectric transducer-receiver application in comparison with the PTCa/P(VDF-TrFE) with 65 vol% ceramic loading.

articleTitle: Influence of the polarizing electrode material on the space charge storage in low density polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The influence of the polarizing electrode material on the storage of space charge in low density polyethylene (LDPE) was studied using the thermal step technique. Test samples were discs of 1.9 mm thickness provided with different types of electrodes: vacuum deposited gold and aluminium, plasma enhanced chemical vapour deposited silicon carbide (SiC), and pressed aluminium disc electrodes. Space charge was formed using 50 kV de voltage for 72 hours at two different temperatures 25/spl deg/C and 50/spl deg/C. Results indicate that the distribution of space charge density through the sample is dependent on the type of the electrode material, the nature of electrode/polymer interface and temperature of space charge formation.

articleTitle: Hopping electronic conduction and long-term relaxation of an electret state in disordered dielectrics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The paper presents the results of investigating the isothermal relaxation of an electret potential difference U/sub e/ which is due to the screening of the surface charge of injected carriers in the bulk of a dielectric. Considering the hopping transport mechanism it can be explained why the decay time of U/sub e/ is much greater than the Maxwell relaxation time. The suggested model allows one to determine from experimental data some important parameters of disordered dielectrics. Among these parameters are the density of localized electrons, the scattering of localized electronic states in energy and Fermi level energy. Experimental data for U/sub e/ vs. time dependence for amorphous tantalum oxide are compared with those predicted from the model.

articleTitle: Generation mechanism of pressure pulse wave using piezoelectric transducer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The pressure wave propagation method using a piezoelectrically generated pressure pulse has been applied to the research of charge behavior in a dielectric. In this paper, the generation mechanism of the pressure pulse wave by using a piezoelectric transducer is investigated. The results show that the generated pressure pulse has been described by using a simple convolutional equation.

articleTitle: A new method to study processes of corona charging and electric relaxation in electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The idea of the proposed method is in the analysis of the experimentally obtained response (electret potential) of the dielectric sample on application of the rectangular current pulses of infra-low frequency. The current is supplied by a corona, and the whole process of the poling (electrization) splits into a number of separate fractions, each consisting of the stage of the potential growth under the constant charging current and the stage of the potential decay in the gap between the two adjacent current pulses. The corresponding formulae are derived allowing to follow the dynamics of the dielectric constant and the apparent conductivity with evolution of the poling process. The method is applied to study corona charging and electric relaxation in PVDF, although it is applicable in principle to any dielectric with a reasonable apparent conductivity.

articleTitle: Pyro- and piezoelectricity in sol-gel derived ceramic/polymer composites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Electroactive ceramic/polymer composites with 0-3 connectivity pattern have been studied recently in view of their attractive properties for smart sensors applications. Sol-gel processing is a convenient technique to obtain ceramics of high purity and molecular homogeneity. A further advantage is the use of lower processing temperatures than that of the conventional mixed oxides route. In this work we have synthesized lead titanate (PT) and calcium modified lead titanate (PTCa) ceramic powders by this technique. Various techniques have been used to evaluate the characteristics of the resulting ceramics.

articleTitle: Generalization of initial rise methods for TSC and TL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Initial rise methods are one of the simplest and most credible ones for evaluating trap parameters in TSC (thermally stimulated conductivity) and TL (thermoluminescence) experimental techniques. In those methods, it is assumed, that during linear heating, for a small initial part of TSC or TL peak, the intensity J is proportional to exp(-E/kT), where E is the activation energy of a trap. In this work we derive new generalized equations for TSC and TL in the form of "initial rise" equation with a new "correction term" added. These equations were tested numerically for different trap parameters. In most cases the fit error was less than 0.1% in the whole range of the spectrum.

articleTitle: Solid state electret microphones
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A novel solid state electret microphone is proposed in this paper. The distinguishing feature of this device compared with analogous subminiature microphones is application of silicon frames, silicon membranes and inorganic silicon based electret layers. The proposed microphones are made using micromechanical and microelectronical techniques already employed in fabrication of static pressure sensors. Charging of the electret layer is performed after the complete fabrication of the microphone chip.

articleTitle: Corona charging of polypropylene films in the atmosphere of hydrogen
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Corona triode has been used for studying charge storage and transport properties of polypropylene (PP) films in controlled atmosphere of hydrogen. Studies of charging transient currents (I-t) and isochronal current-voltage (I-V) characteristics for one-side metallized samples are reported. Space charge limited currents, Schottky, Poole-Frenkel and hopping conductivity are discussed. The open-circuit thermally stimulated currents after positive and negative corona charging are also presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear charging and polarization phenomena in thin polymeric layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The build-up of the heterocharge and nonlinear effects of polarization and charging in thin polymeric layers polyethylene terephthalate has been studied by us at polarization temperatures 160-190/spl deg/C. The nature of nonlinear effects is discussed on the basis of different models.

articleTitle: High field conduction and breakdown of ultra thin evaporated polypropylene films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The conduction current of an Al/thin PP film/Al structure are explained by tunneling injection and its breakdown strength was about 12 MV/cm without a self-healing breakdown. The surface structures of a conventional PP film and a thin PP film were measured with ESCA, and compared with each other. The degree of oxidation of the thin PP film surface was two times higher than that of a conventional PP film surface. X-ray diffraction studies showed that the thin PP film had high crystallinity and orientation.

articleTitle: Effects of repeated polarization reversal on polarization properties in vinylidene fluoride trifluoroethylene copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Vinylidene fluoride/trifluoroethylene copolymers are suitable materials to produce a memory device. In the case of this device, information is stored in the polarity of the polarization. It has been reported that the remnant polarization decays with an increase in the reversal period. Now we present the effect of the reversal condition on the hysteresis properties. It became obvious that the property changes are related to the fraction of the reversed polarization. Furthermore the effect in the condition of restriction and distribution of the polarization are discussed.

articleTitle: Application of Gauss quadrature formula to calculation of thermally stimulated current
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In order to calculate the activation energy of dipole relaxation and electron detrapping, it is necessary to estimate thermally stimulated current (TSC) I(T). One generally uses the asymptotic series to express the exponential integral in TSC. Its main inconvenience is that for n/spl rarr//spl infin/, each term goes to infinity. Although this series has properties that permit a very good approximation for exponential integral, it is divergent. For the above reasons we use a Gauss quadrature formula to estimate the exponential integral. Its marked characteristics are: high precision, fast convergence and good stability. We have applied this formula to the estimation of the activation energy of charge carrier in traps in TSC data of R. Chen.

articleTitle: Dielectric and conductivity studies of cyclodextrins
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Dielectric and conductivity studies of /spl alpha/- and /spl beta/-cyclodextrins, their derivatives and inclusion complexes with various guest molecules, have been performed by AC spectroscopic techniques in the frequency range 10 Hz-1 GHz and the temperature range -11 to 23/spl deg/C. A dispersion appearing in all cases is displaced towards the lower frequencies with decreasing temperature and its overall behaviour depends markedly on the CD type, the degree of substitution, the nature of the guest molecule and the water content of the CD sample. The activation energy and the pre-exponential factor of the relaxation mechanism have been evaluated in the various cases and the results are discussed in comparison with data obtained with the same or identical samples by the same authors with the TSDC technique (ISE7) and with data reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents in quartz and mixed alkali silicate glasses
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) technique was used to monitor (in the range 100-620 K) the dielectric relaxations of (1) silica glasses of different origin and impurity contents (mainly Al and OH) and (2) soda-lime silicate (SLS) glasses, in which K/sup +/ and Ag/sup +/ were also substituted for Na/sup +/. In the SLS glasses three TSDC bands appear at temperatures lower than the main band of SiO/sub 2/ specimens: the position of two peaks depends on the nature of the monovalent ion. The polarization phenomena were larger in SLS than in SiO/sub 2/ glasses. The peak position and amplitudes were studied as a function of the polarization field, temperature and time. The origin of the relaxations is discussed.

articleTitle: Direct correlations between mechanical-relaxation measurements. Differential-scanning-calorimetry data, and thermally stimulated charge-decay results from Teflon-FEP electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Commercial Teflon-FEP films from DuPont were studied by means of several different techniques: The complex shear modulus was measured with a torsion pendulum at 1 Hz between -180 and +260/spl deg/C; the complex dielectric permittivity was studied between 100 Hz and 1 MHz from -150 to +300/spl deg/C; differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to determine the phase transitions in the temperature range from -150 to +300/spl deg/C. The results are compared to reported thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) curves for the same polymer. It is found that the known TSD peaks around -80/spl deg/C, around +80/spl deg/C, and above +200/spl deg/C are closely matched by corresponding features of the mechanical, dielectric, and calorimetric measurements which are ascribed to relaxations at the /spl beta/ or glass II transition, at the /spl alpha/ or glass I transition, and in the premelting region, respectively. While the origin of these TSD peaks from movements of the polymer molecules is quite certain, the TSD peak around +155/spl deg/C found on negatively surface-charged samples requires apparently a more complex explanation. Since the TSD peaks of positively and negatively charged electrets from the other Teflons (PTFE, PFA, and AT) are often found at the same temperatures, their respective discharge-current peaks may have the same physical origins.

articleTitle: A stochastic charge carrier transport model applied to the surface potential kinetics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Starting from a microscopic model of an electret, we study a nonlinear partial differential equation describing the space charge evolution process. Under definite initial and boundary conditions the charge transport equation is solved explicity in the small signal case, and the surface potential kinetics are derived. This leads to estimates of the electret conductivity and the concentration of the localized states.

articleTitle: Effect of acetophenone coating on carrier injection into polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The existence of acetophenone at the electrode interfaces significantly enhance the high field dc conduction current in LDPE film. This effect was more remarkable when acetophenone was put on the positive gold electrode or negative aluminum electrode. These results show that the acetophenone enhances the electronic carrier injection into polyethylene, especially holes for gold electrode and electrons for aluminum electrode, probably modifying the surface state at the electrode interface. The result on the effect of polarity reversal suggests the injected carriers before the polarity reversal act as a hetero-space charge after the polarity reversal and enhance the carrier injection.

articleTitle: Radiation-induced suppression of charge injection into low density polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally stimulated conductivity (TSC) and thermally stimulated depolarisation (TSD) current measurements have been used to study the effects of X-irradiation on charge injection into thin films of low density polyethylene. It was found that, for evaporated gold electrodes and a nominal applied field strength of 100 kV/cm, charge injection into an unirradiated sample commences around -50/spl deg/C, passes through a maximum around -20/spl deg/C, falls to a minimum around 0/spl deg/C and then increases rapidly. An X-ray dose of 12 kGy at room temperature appeared to suppress charge injection at temperatures below about 30/spl deg/C. The TSD curves of X-irradiated samples showed a new peak around 90/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear conductive spectra of ion-conducting polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The linear and nonlinear complex conductivities have been measured as a function of frequency for the polyethylene oxide modified by the addition of SiO/sub 2/, or doped with LiClO/sub 4/. The observed spectra exhibit marked conductive relaxation, suggesting the existence of different conduction processes in the low-frequency regions. It was found that combinations of the linear and nonlinear conductivities as given by the dynamic percolation theory allow estimates of a hopping distance without any additional assumptions. It was also suggested that the elementary process of the ion transport in the ion-conducting polymers was caused by ion hopping between available sites, and therefore, the typical size of a cluster of available sites is about 4 nm.

articleTitle: High pressure applications of ferroelectric polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Ferroelectric polymers are the most recent class piezoelectric and pyroelectric materials developed. The most common piezoelectric polymers are PVDF, based on the monomer CH/sub 2/-CF2 and copolymers PVDF with C/sub 2/F/sub 3/H. Under high hydrostatic pressure, piezoelectric polymers exhibit well defined piezoelectric response. Piezoelectric response of shock compressed PVDF film prepared with attention to mechanical and electrical processing exhibits precise, well defined reproducible behavior to 35 GPa. P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers exhibit unique piezoelectric properties over a wide range of temperature depending on the compositions. Under high shock pressure loading. Unique piezoelectric response is also observed. In particular, a first record of detonation profile is presented. These polymers have the potential for new shock wave sensors with unique characteristics.

articleTitle: The electroacoustic waves and its symmetry in anti-parallel polarising multilayer structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The dispersion characteristics of the ferroelectric domain layer waves (FDLW) in the 180/spl deg/ domain structure of PZT-5 materials with finite layers have been discussed in the paper. Comparing with some 180/spl deg/ domain structure, a new FDLW mode with asymmetric vibration is found. Experimental results are agreement with the theoretical ones. In the other, it is shown theoretically that the electromechanical coupling factor of the FDLW mode in the 180/spl deg/ domain sandwich structure increases rapidly as hk decreases at hk/spl Lt/1.

articleTitle: Possible protonic conduction in Teflon FEP under humid atmospheres
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Studies of constant current corona, negatively charged Teflon FEP samples, show a surface potential build up depending on the humidity content. In dry air atmospheres it is possible to charge a sample to very high charge densities. In humid atmospheres the surface potential saturates at lower potentials. Charge centroid position measurements show that in samples charged under humid conditions the centroid position is deeper than in the case of dry conditions. On the other hand, surface charge decays much faster in humid atmospheres than in dry air. These results are explained in terms of a protonic model for charge transport, in Teflon FEP under humid conditions, in which the negative surface charges induce a drift of ions from the bulk to the surface charge layer.

articleTitle: Space charge measurement in XLPE cable insulation under high field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Space charge distribution was measured applying an electric field of over 1 MV/cm to 3-mm thick XLPE cable insulation. Under a high field, hetero charges were formed soon after voltage application, followed by an injection from the cathode. Then intermittent injections of charge packet from the anode took place. The space charge distribution kept changing without becoming stabilized. A simulation was done assuming hysteresis of the injection characteristics due to instability near the anode.

articleTitle: Ferroelectric switching characteristics of nylon 11
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The time-domain measurement of polarization reversal has been made for melt-quenched and uniaxially-drawn nylon 11. An application of a high step electric field is found to induce a fast switching of remnant polarization 40 mC/m/sup 2/ being independent of the field strength in the 120-240 MV/m range. The switching time depends upon the field strength according to an exponential law. Extrapolating to an infinite field yields a switching time of 1 /spl mu/s. As the field is decreased, polarization reversal is obscured to disappear below 40 MV/m and the field dependence of the switching time is transferred to a power law. These results conclude that nylon 11 is a ferroelectric polymer analogous to vinylidene fluoride copolymers.

articleTitle: In-situ pyroelectrical study of the polarization dynamics in nonlinear optical polymers and physico-chemical investigation of photo-induced degradation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The photo-isomerization of azo-chromophores in a nonlinear optical side-chain polymer permits the orientation of the dipoles under an applied electric field even well below the glass-transition temperature of the polymer. As the dipoles become orientable only within the penetration depth of the pump light, the technique is especially suitable for the preparation of poling patterns across the thickness of the polymer. Pyroelectrical investigations allow for an in-situ examination of the photo-induced poling process and for an analysis of the resulting nonuniform dipole-orientation patterns. For long-time exposures to the short-wavelength pump light, a photo-induced degradation of the chromophore molecules (photo-bleaching) is observed, which is analyzed by pyroelectrical (thermal) analysis, optical techniques and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Dielectric investigation of polypropylene grafted with maleic anhydride
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The blends of pure polypropylene and 3 wt% maleic anhydride grafted polypropylene have been investigated by means of dielectric and conductive spectroscopy. Since the blends are nearly nonpolar, they exhibit a very weak dielectric relaxation near room temperature associated with the glass transition. Linear relation between the relaxation strength and the maleic anhydride content allows an estimate of the dipole moment of maleic anhydride to yield 2.3D. The dc conductivity is found to become a minimum at 5 wt% grafted polypropylene. It is suggested that an introduction of a small amount of polar groups into a nonpolar polymer supply charge traps to reduce its conductivity.

articleTitle: Correlations between pyroelectricity, thermal transitions and dielectric relaxations in PVDF and related copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The temperature dependence of the pyroelectric coefficient of PVDF and P(VDF-TrFE)75/25 has been correlated with thermal transitions and dielectric relaxations as revealed by DSC and TSC. For both polymers, three changes in slope have been found: the lower temperature one corresponds to the glass transition of the free amorphous phase of the polymers. An upper component of the glass transition, Tgu(10/20/spl deg/C) has been ascribed to the glass transition of the amorphous phase constrained by crystallites. The /spl alpha/ process occurs at 40/50/spl deg/C. It has been associated with conformational reorganizations related to the crystalline phase. It plays a key role in ageing of electroactive properties. Above T/spl alpha/, cooperative movements are liberated. They are precursors of the Curie transition.

articleTitle: Transport of injected charge through an insulator with a distribution of trapping capture and release times
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The transport of injected charge of one polarity through an insulator containing a uniform spatial distribution of carrier traps has been computer-simulated. The capture/release-time distributions for trapping are both variable. The injection mechanisms are (a) saturated space-charge-limited-current (SCLC), (b) diffusion-limited thermionic injection, and (c) as in (b) but without the diffusion limitation. Recent experimental data for polyethylene showing j/spl prop/E/sup n/, where j is the steady-state current density, E is the applied field, and n=4-6, are shown to be inconsistent with a SCLC regime and a distribution of trapping/release-times.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of charge storage in corona charged polyethylene film
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: For some fluoropolymer films, such as Teflon FEP etc., their charge stability can be remarkably improved by the application of heat during corona charging, but polyethylene (PE) is an exception. In this paper, the behavior of corona charged PE film at elevated temperatures was studied. Using the phenomenological model derived by R.L. Remke et al. (1983), the attempt-to-escape frequencies and detrapping time constant at RT were estimated for PE, Teflon PTFE, FEP and PFA. By means of the comparison, the performance of the charge storage for PE sample was evaluated.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo simulation of TSC and TL in spatially correlated systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Numerical calculations were performed to study the kinetics of charge carriers' trapping and recombination in systems, where traps and recombination centres are spatially correlated. A new Monte Carlo algorithm was developed for systems with traps that are not fulfilled initially. The dependence of TSC and TL spectra on initial filling ratio were studied. It is shown, that for low initial filling ratios thermally stimulated relaxation spectra strongly depend on spatial correlation.

articleTitle: Space charge and dielectric breakdown in polypropylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Quantitative probing of space charge and breakdown strength measurements were carried out on polypropylene (PP) at room temperature. A positive space charge due to injection was formed at low fields. Electrons are injected and form a homo space charge either in the high field region or when the cathode field is enhanced by the positive space charge extended from the anode. It was concluded that at room temperature the breakdown is initiated by the injected electrons and it mainly takes place in the region near the cathode. Effects of physical structure on the space charge behaviour is also under investigation.

articleTitle: Thermally stable highly efficient electro-optic polymer modulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Design and fabrication of low-loss nonlinear polymer waveguides with attenuation smaller than 2 dB/cm are reported. Electro-optic devices based on this polymer such as phase modulators and Mach-Zehnder interferometers, have been fabricated and demonstrated. The best figures obtained so far at 1.32 /spl mu/m are V/sub /spl pi//=10 V for the phase modulator inserted between crossed polarizers and V/sub /spl pi//=9 V for the Mach-Zehnder modulator working in TM polarization. The electro-optic polymer is stable at 85/spl deg/C for more than 2000 hours.

articleTitle: Electrical and mechanical effects on the transport phenomena in polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Electrical conductivity of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films was studied as a function of hydrostatic pressure P from 50 to 500 bars at T=100/spl deg/C over a range of field F up to 2 MV/cm. It is found that the current density increases with F and decreases with P. Analysis of the conductivity variations showed that ionic conduction in PET is predominant by using Miyamoto's model.

articleTitle: Polymer surface electric properties modification by plasma corrosion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally Stimulated Discharge Current method, TSDC, was used to analyze the surface modification of poly(ethylene terephthalate), PET, as a consequence of plasma corrosion of the sample. The interaction between a low pressure gas plasma and organic materials has mechanical (surface cleaning and dry micro-etching) and electrostatic (cross-linking) and surface activation effects. These effects conduct to changes in polymer surface electrical properties. The measurements were made on as received sample, electron injected sample and polarized sample.
