The peak's position and peak's intensity changes depend on the corrosion conditions and electric charging procedure. The injected charge is less stable than the polarization charge. If the corrosion time is long or the corrosion energy is high, the sample dielectric breakdown strength decreases.

articleTitle: Charge stability of teflon-FEP electrets charged at melting temperatures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: To reach as high charge stability as possible we tried to charge FEP at temperatures in the melting region. Therefore the foil was heat sealed on a metal plate. After charging the samples were also thermally aged at melting temperature in some experiments. Charge stability was investigated by thermally stimulated charge decay (TSCD) and thermally stimulated current in open circuit (TSC-O).

articleTitle: Charge storage and transport behaviour of pure and anthracene doped poly methyl methacrylate (PMMA) foils
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The charge storage and transport behaviour of bimetallized, 100 /spl mu/m thick, pure and anthracene doped poly methyl methacrylate (PMMA) foils has been studied by investigating dark conduction currents, transient absorption currents and thermally stimulated depolarization (TSD) over a wide temperature range of 298 to 393 K, with fields ranging from 8 to 50 kV/cm.

articleTitle: Analysis of vapor-phase deposited polydichloro-p-xylylene (PDCPX) film electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper, a new kind of vapor-phase deposited polydichloro-p-xylylene (PDCPX) electrets is analysed. The electret film is formed in vacuum by depositing vapor-phase PDCPX on the surface of metal materials. We charged the sample by the usual methods. It is supposed that ohmic conduction has contribution to the short circuit thermally stimulated discharge of the samples, and a non-Debye response of polarization decay possibly exists.

articleTitle: Study by thermally stimulated current spectroscopy of radiation damage to skin
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to characterize the effects of radiation on collagen and skin by thermally stimulated current (TSC) spectroscopy. X-rays, /spl beta/-rays and UV radiation have similar effects on the molecular mobility of dermal collagen and skin. They induce the decrease of magnitude of the intra and intermolecular mobilities. The restriction of the molecular movements can be explained by an increase of collagen cross links.

articleTitle: Dielectric study of the denaturation process in albumin-urea solutions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The dielectric relaxation of bovine serum albumin (BSA) aqueous solution was studied in various stages of urea denaturation, by means of the Thermally Stimulated Depolarization Currents (TSDC) technique. A large variation of urea concentration was utilized (0 to 4 M). Special attention was given to concentrations 0.006 and 0.046 M which are comparable to the ones measured in normal and uremic human serum. Three spectral bands were recorded in the temperature range 77 to 300 K which are attributed to the reorientation mechanisms of bulk and hydration water and protein macromolecules. The activation energies for all three mechanisms appear to be dependent on urea concentration and this result is discussed in terms of the conformational changes of albumin upon denaturation.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated discharge and polarization currents in aromatic polyamides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Studies carried out on the Thermally Stimulated Discharge (TSD) and Thermally Stimulated Polarization (TSP) currents in aromatic polyamides are presented. TSD currents are measured at various poling fields, duration of poling. Annealing time and rate of heating during release of charges. The currents show a peak at 135/spl deg/C for a rate of heating of 1 k/min and the peak shifts to a higher value with increase of rate of heating. Thermally stimulated polarization currents are also measured and the influence of various parameters are investigated. The results show that a dipolar process is applicable which is replaced by interfacial polarization as the temperature is increased. The latter is the predominant mechanism at 200/spl deg/C, which is in agreement with the charging current measurements in the same material.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy in blends of polyurethane and styrene-acrylonitrile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Blends of polyurethanes based on branched polymer polyol (PUR) and styrene-acrylonitrile copolymers (SAN), with different SAN content and different SAN compositions in acrylonitrile (AN)/styrene (St), were studied, by using different dielectric relaxation spectroscopy techniques, in order to investigate interactions between the components of the blends. The dielectric behaviour of the blends showed that the two components of the blends are incompatible. No significant interactions between SAN and soft polyol segments of the PUR have been observed, while there was evidence that SAN interacts with hard segments affecting the segmentation of soft and hard domains of the PUR. These interactions seem to be dependent on the composition of SAN in AN/St.

articleTitle: A study of dielectric relaxation time with pressure for vitamin D-3 in powder form
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this work, a sample of vitamin D/sub 3/ in wafer form prepared by special technique and subjected to different pressures in the range of 5 to 8 tons, subjected to high frequency perturbations in the range 10 to 30 MHz yield the relaxation times in the range of 7.58 n sec to 14.47 n sec. The results are explained on the basis of existing theories and the recent results of Li Shengtao et al. (1991) and Manabu Takeuchi (1991).

articleTitle: The role of high pressure in the study and applications of the ferroelectric polymer polyvinylidene fluoride and its copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The effects of frequency, temperature and hydrostatic pressure on the dielectric properties, molecular relaxations, and phase transitions of PVDF and a copolymer with 30 mol% trifluoroethylene will be discussed. Pressure causes large slowing down of the /spl beta/ molecular relaxations as well as large increases in the ferroelectric transition temperatures and melting points, but the magnitudes of the effects are different for the different "transitions." These effects can be understood in terms of pressure-induced hindrance of the molecular motions and/or reorientations. A unique application of these polymers as time-resolved dynamic stress gauges based on PVDF studies under very high pressure shock compression is discussed.

articleTitle: Kinetics of radiation-induced conductivity and thermally-stimulated currents in disordered dielectrics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Kinetics of radiation-induced conductivity (RIG) in disordered dielectrics is considered. The results obtained for the dispersive hopping RIC are similar to those obtained for trap-controlled RIG. This permits to understand why the model of trap-controlled transport and recombination is able to explain many experimentally observed characteristic features of carrier transport and RIC in materials in which transport is not governed by extended states. Thermally-stimulated currents in disordered hopping systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Electrical and dielectric measurements in conducting poly(ethylene oxide)-based electrolytes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: We report on electrical and dielectrical measurements on several PEO-salt complexes (pure PEO and PEO with 5 and 18% KSCN, 1 and 5% Ba(SCN)/sub 2/, 3 and 18% NaSCN, 10% KBr, compositions given in terms of the proportion in moles between the polymer repeat unit (-CH/sub 2/CH/sub 2/O-) and the salt) by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC), polarization currents (TSPC), DC conductivity techniques in the temperature range 77-300 K and of impedance spectroscopy techniques (5 Hz-13 MHz, 200-400 K). Four relaxation mechanisms have been detected. The main relaxation mechanism associated with the glass transition is studied in some detail. The glass transition shifts to higher temperatures by complexation.

articleTitle: Similarities between pressure wave propagation and photopyroelectric spectroscopic techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The Pressure Wave Pulse (PWP) technique is a powerful method used to determine electric polarization profile in films of polymeric materials, and the Photopyroelectric Spectroscopy (PPES) has been applied with a great success in the study of thermal and optical properties of semiconductor and glass materials. In this article we show that the PWP and the PPES are equally useful techniques to investigate, respectively, the charge distribution of poled soda-lime glass and thermal and optical parameters of polymer films. Some similarities, as well as some differences, of these techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: Electric conductivity of ethylene propylene copolymer: effect of alumina
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The dependence of the electric conductivity, /spl sigma/, on the electric field, E, was measured on ethylene propylene (EPDM) copolymer with and without alumina filler. It was found that a Schottky-like charge injection process conjugated to a modified Poole-Frenkel model for the bulk conduction was necessary for accounting the experimental results for samples without alumina filler. However, the experimental results for samples with alumina filler showed that the conductivity /spl sigma/ depends also on the sample thickness suggesting a space-charge perturbed bulk conduction.

articleTitle: Influence of irradiation on electrical properties of conducting polymer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Electrical properties of electron beam irradiated polypyrrole films, which are conducting polymer, were studied. Conductivity increased with increasing the temperature from -190/spl deg/C to 180/spl deg/C. The conductivity was constant from 0 Gy to 50 MGy irradiation, then rapidly decreased from 50 MGy to 150 MGy irradiation. Moreover, free radicals decreased with dose. From the results of chemical analysis, it was found that the numbers of C=C, C-C and C-N bonds decreased with dose.

articleTitle: Time-of-flight concept applied for determination of ion mobility
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Summary form only given. In recent years there has been an increasing interest in using dielectric techniques for in situ monitoring of resin curing processes. These techniques consist in monitoring of changes of ionic conductivity. Although many investigations have been made, difficulties in direct measurements of physical quantities related to ionic conductivity and the complexity of the investigated polymer materials make the interpretation and understanding of the results difficult. Because the key parameter is the ion mobility which is related to the medium viscosity, a direct ion mobility measurements would be of great importance. In the present paper we show, that the time-of-flight (TOF) concept can be used for determination of the changes of the ion mobility in a course of resin curing. The TOF method applied to ions consists of two steps: i) accumulation of mobile ions close to one electrode of the capacitor-type sensor filled with the investigated resin by means of constant electric field applied to the sample; and ii) recording of the transient current caused by a step-like change of the field polarity. In an ideal case the current should be initially constant and then it should decrease rapidly when the ions reach the opposite electrode. Multiple repetition of the above two-step sequence allows one to follow the changes of the transient times during the resin curing. The measurements were carried for the well known DGEBA/3DCM epoxy/amine system cured isothermally at different temperatures. It was found, that the ionic mobility decreases linearly with the conductivity up to the gelation point. Then the conductivity starts to decay faster. Parallel TOF measurements show that this decrease is only partially caused by the decay of ionic mobility; it means that simultaneously the concentration of the mobile ions decreases also. The obtained results prove usefulness of the TOF method for studies of ionic conductivity.

articleTitle: TSC and DSC measurements of polymeric insulators used in medium voltage distribution cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: This article describes results of thermally stimulated current (TSC) measurements of XLPE, HDPE and PVC samples, which are used as insulating materials in medium voltage cables used in electrical energy distribution. Systematic investigations have been made in order to correlate physical parameters of charge storage with the breakdown phenomena observed in voltage tracking resistance tests (VTR). Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements were also performed in order to verify if some of the TSC peaks arise from relaxation processes associated with eventual morphological and/or structural modifications. A correlation is shown between material conductivity and voltage tracking resistance.

articleTitle: On the role of charge injection and trapping in stability of polarization in ferroelectric polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The experimental results are presented on anomalous behavior of absorption currents in PVDF during the stepwise increase of the voltage applied through a corona. These results, supplemented with the dynamics of the time constant of the electret potential decay, are consistent with a hypothesis assuming a deep trapping of the charge carriers during the polarization buildup in ferroelectric polymers. The model calculations are made on a distribution of the potential energy at the surface of the polarized crystallites, proving that additional sites for the charge trapping are created there. It Is shown how to provide the most favourable conditions for obtaining a stable polarization in ferroelectric polymers.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction in ferrocene mixed polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The electrical transport behaviour of ferrocene mixed polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) films (approximately 20 microns in thickness) deposited by the isothermal immersion technique has been studied in the temperature range of 333-373 K and field from (2.0-4.0)/spl times/10/sup 4/ volts/cm. It has been found that at higher fields and temperatures, the observed conduction behaviour could be consistently described by the Richardson-Schottky emission. Increase in current due to doping has been attributed the formation of charge transfer complexes. The dopant molecules acts as an additional trapping centre and provide a link between polymer molecules in the amorphous region leading to the formation of a charge transfer complex.

articleTitle: Switching transients in an ultrathin ferroelectric copolymer film
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The switching characteristics of P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer films, with a thickness of 50 nm, have been measured at room temperature. The spontaneous polarisation is around 29 mCm/sup -2/ and the duration of the switching current varies from about 50 /spl mu/s to 150 /spl mu/s for fields varying from 200 MV m/sup -1/ to 300 MV m/sup -1/. The switching current can be analysed using a domain nucleation and growth theory. The results indicate that domain nucleation may be inhibited by injected charge.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric parameters of polymer films obtained from resonance-antiresonance pyroelectric response
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Pyroelectric response of nonuniformly polarized PVDF type films is accompanied by pyroelectric resonance related to vibration mode of bending type. The pyroelectric resonance method was applied to determine piezoelectric parameters of PVDF polymer films of various origin.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of piezoelectric constants for polyureas synthesized by vapor deposition polymerization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thin films of aromatic and aliphatic polyureas are prepared by the evaporation and deposition of a diamine monomer and a diisocyanate monomer onto a polyimide substrate in a vacuum chamber. Application of a high electric field induces the films a residual polarization due to the alignment of urea bond dipoles. The piezoelectric constants for aromatic polyureas are almost unchanged from -150/spl deg/C to 200/spl deg/C. While those for aromatic polyureas show relaxational change due to the thermal molecular motions.

articleTitle: Investigation of structures and properties of dc magnetic control reactive sputtering deposited Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ electret films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: By studying the effects of sputtering current and pressure of gas on the growth rate and quality of Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ thin films, we have obtained the following optimum technical parameters: sputtering current-0.6 A; oxygen pressure lower than 3 Pa (for such conditions, the sputtering rate is greater than 64 nm/min.); even and homogeneous film. Using XRD, TEM and SEM measurements, the change of film structure was observed before and after annealing at high temperature. Using XPS, the chemical structure and composition of the Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ surface was analysed. It is experimentally shown that this film after annealling possesses multicrystalline structure containing Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ and TaO along (0001) as a textured direction, and excellent electrical, chemical, piezoelectric and sensitive properties.

articleTitle: Mechanical stresses and charge stability in non-polar polymeric electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A correlation between morphology and charge stability in non-polar polymeric electrets has been studied. It has been possible to show that isometric heating of polymer led to the changes in the supermolecular structure, particularly in the crystallinity. Electret measurements were made using special experimental method, based on simultaneous registration of the thermal shrinkage stresses and the surface potential relaxation. It has been found that mechanical stresses in the polymer influenced on the charge stability significantly. From the results obtained we were able to determine the isometric heating conditions which were useful to improve charge stability of non-polar polymeric electrets.

articleTitle: Blends of PVDF and a conducting polymer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Blends of poly(vinylidene fluoride)-PVDF and-poly(o-methoxyaniline)-POMA-of various compositions were produced by casting in dimethylformamide (DMF). Flexible films were obtained which were characterized, using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, two-probe conductivity, dielectric polarization, thermo-stimulated current (TSC) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). As expected, the blends conductivity increases considerably with increasing contents of doped POMA. These polymer blends possess conductivity in a wide range what may be seen as a new class of semiconductors. The influence of the conducting polymer on the characteristics of PVDF is discussed.

articleTitle: Space charge build-up and transport in thin dielectric films: a new approach based on electroluminescence detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A new way is presented for deriving space charge dynamics and transport parameters in thin films sandwiched between two metallic electrodes. The measurement method uses the detection of the electroluminescence excited by square voltage pulses. In this conference, we report on hydrogenated amorphous carbon layers synthesised by gas phase polymerisation. The space charge build-up time is derived from the electroluminescence time lag when the structure is excited by a single square voltage pulse. The relaxation time of the space charge is investigated by using a double pulse excitation. An optical transit-time technique is proposed to determine the carrier mobility.

articleTitle: Some features of the electric relaxation in PVDF and PVDF-PZT composites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: It is shown that relaxation of the residual polarization in PVDF can be caused by spontaneous switching of a portion of the polarized volume to its initial electric state. The phenomenon is observed as Barkhausen's pulses. The duration of the pulse, the magnitude of a leap, and the switched volume per pulse are calculated. The current oscillations of infra-low frequency are also observed in partly poled samples, caused by a propagation of polarization waves (solitons) through the sample thickness. It is shown that relaxation of the unstable component of the residual polarization is responsible for the thermally stimulated currents in PVDF-PZT composites. The thermally stable one provides for the piezo- and pyroelectricity in the composite.

articleTitle: Trapping phenomena and supermolecular structure of polyester electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Polyethylene naphthalate dicarboxylate (PEN) films with various degrees of planar orientation were prepared by uniaxial and biaxial stretching. A linear relationship between the mean trap depth calculated from Thermally Stimulated Current spectra and the degree of planar orientation was observed. The structural origin of local states of PEN electret was proposed after X-ray diffraction measurement.

articleTitle: Voltage control of molecular diffusion through novel liquid crystalline membranes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A preliminary investigation into the behaviour of a novel polymer membrane containing an embedded liquid crystal under the influence of very low (1 V/mm) DC and AC 100 Hz electric field stresses has been carried out. The rate of diffusion of methylene blue in an aqueous solution with applied electrical stress is reported. The results suggest that the rate of diffusion of methylene blue through the membrane can be controlled by the polarity of an applied DC voltage and by the application of a sinusoidal AC field.

articleTitle: Melt-solidified and cast films of P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers: a comparison study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Structural and electrical properties of poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluorethylene)P(VDF-TrFE) films, obtained either from casting a solution or by compression moulding from a molten phase, have been reported in a number of studies. Even though results may differ to a considerable extent when samples are prepared with different methods, few studies address these differences whose origins may lie in distinct thermal treatments. In the present study we undertake a careful comparison of experimental DSC and FTIR results on 60/40, 70/30 and 80/20 P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer samples, fabricated using these two methods. The DSC results for the 60/40 and 70/30 copolymer show two phase transitions, with the samples behaving as a paraelectric material only after the 2nd transition. It is shown that the main differences between melt-solidified and cast films arise from the thermal treatment suffered by the former samples.

articleTitle: X-ray radiation-induced conductivity in both ferro and paraelectric phase of P(VDF/TrFE) copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: An investigation of the radiation-induced conductivity (RIC) in P(VDF/TrFE) copolymer of 70:30 molar ratio, due to X-ray irradiation, was performed at different temperatures. At room temperature (ferroelectric phase) the RIC presented a quasi-linear dependence on time even after three hours of continuous irradiation, for dose rates of approximately 10 Gy/s. At 120/spl deg/C, in the paraelectric phase, the RIC was linear in the first minutes of irradiation, leached a maximum at about 10 minutes and then decreased slowly. The results were explained in terms of a dispersive transport mechanism, and the Arkhipov model was used to fit the experimental data.

articleTitle: Thermal polarization mechanisms on 0-3 type ferroelectric composites based on PVDF
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The 0-3 type composites of TGS, BaTiO/sub 3/ and LiNbO/sub 3/ crystal, BaTiO/sub 3/ and PZT ceramics based on PVDF have been prepared. The long term polarization relaxation in the composites been studied. This indicates that there are three mechanisms with different relaxation times. These mechanisms result from crystalline grains of the crystal or ceramics, matrix and grain boundaries. The stable polarization results from the grain boundaries.

articleTitle: Characterization of the influence of processing conditions on polarization phenomena in PVC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The Thermally Stimulated Current (TSC) spectroscopy has been applied to the characterization of the influence of processing conditions on polarization phenomena of PVC. Two relaxation modes are observed, independently from the thermomechanical history of the polymer. Both modes can be described by continuous distribution of relaxation times following a compensation law. So, each mode has been characterized by a compensation time and the range of the activation enthalpies. The compensation temperature is particularly sensitive to the thermomechanical history of the polymer and to the presence of lubricants and plasticizers.

articleTitle: Transport, injection and storage of electric charges in alumina (Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/) single crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper we describe the application of the pressure wave propagation method to the non-destructive measurement of the space charge dynamics in Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ single crystals, under high voltage, at room temperature. A build up of a positive space charge in the vicinity of the anode is observed, and a mechanism is proposed to explain the origin of this charge.

articleTitle: New aspects concerning isothermal current and voltage measurement on electrets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Isothermal current and voltage measurements were done on poly(ethylene terephthalate), (PET), to obtain information about charge storage and discharging current mechanism. The discharging current has three characteristic zones. The first zone fits well with the Maxwell relaxation function. The last zone offers important information concerning the most stable stored charge. The discharging of the sample on internal resistance plays a minor role. If the external resistance is higher than the internal resistance, the voltage on the sample increases in time and the logarithmic plot is a straight line for not too long Fp time intervals. A new experimental procedure is proposed for measuring the most stable stored charge. The total charge flowing through the circuit during the polarization is almost equal with the total charge released from the sample.

articleTitle: Transitions of crystalline 1,3,5-trichloro-2,4,6-trimethylbenzene by thermally stimulated current
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The present paper reports the results of thermally stimulated current TSC spectroscopy on 1,3,5-trichloro-2,4,6-trimethylbenzene (TCTMB). We have investigated the relaxation phenomena between liquid nitrogen temperature and 80/spl deg/C covering the two stable solid phases III and IV. The phase behaviour of TCTMB is very complicated because the phase transitions are dependent both on temperature and on time in addition to the thermal history of the specimen. A series of TSC complex spectra corresponding to different thermal history has been performed. Results are discussed in relation to the corresponding structure as determined by X-ray diffraction and are compared with differential scanning calorimetry data reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Structure and photoisomerization of spiropyran LB films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Materials such as spiropyran which show reversible photoisomerization has potential importance in molecular optoelectronics and photonics applications. It is, however, not easy to fabricate a stable and well-characterized LB film of the molecules containing large chromophores, and the size change associated with photoisomerization causes an obstacle to the isomerization in a rigid structure of an LB film. We studied the relation among the film preparation conditions such as additives and so on, the film structure and the reversible photoisomerization performance. The structure of spiropyran LB film was successfully controlled by choosing a proper amount of additives and other conditions, and the prepared film showed stable reversible photoisomerization.

articleTitle: Surface potential relaxation in Se-PVDF structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The surface potential relaxation of free surface of polyvinylidenefluoride-tetrafluoroethylene copolymer films which were corona-charged with different metal-dielectric interface conditions particularly in the case of Se sublayer between an electrode and a sample surface is studied. The experimental results are interpreted from the point of view of improving the stability of the electret state of PVDF films for the purpose of the use of that material as an element of energy-independent memory cells or xerographic layers. It is shown that the charge relaxation in PVDF in relatively strong fields is monitored by Schottky emission from the opposite electrode.

articleTitle: The electret properties of SiO/sub 2/ films prepared by sol-gel process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Improved SiO/sub 2/ electret films prepared by the sol-gel process are described. The electret properties of the SiO/sub 2/ films, including charge stability, and transport of negatively detrapped charges in the bulk, were studied. Two models were employed to simulate the growth of acid and base catalysed samples. By applying the image processing technique of SEM photography and electrical conductivity glow curves, it was found that the sol-gel oxide for electret purpose should be prepared in the acid system.

articleTitle: Guest-host polymeric systems as non-linear optical materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The use of a constant current corona triode in probing the orientation of guest-host nonlinear optical polymers is reported. The use of the constant current arrangement provides information on the surface voltage of the thin film samples during the poling cycle. Dopant nonlinear optical molecules in either poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) and polycarbonates show marked differences in the alignment behaviour as monitored by surface voltage changes. In PMMA, the alignment appears to comprise a simple process attributable only to the dipolar dopant. In the polycarbonates, themselves polar electrets, the alignment exhibits more complex behaviour. Simple dipolar dopant alignment is completed before a longer period of chain dipole alignment occurs. These differences may be important in explaining our previous observations of unusual alignment stability in polycarbonate-based guest-host films.

articleTitle: Electrical behaviour of a main chain liquid crystalline copolyester during melting and crystallisation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Dielectric measurements on a main chain liquid crystalline copolyester reveal that during crystallisation or melting no change in dipole activity occurs. However, interfacial polarisation appears during crystallisation, due to charge accumulation near the crystalline interfaces; it disappears when the polymer melts. The ohmic conductivity derived from the dielectric data increases during isothermal crystallisation. Unlike the liquid crystalline polymer, polyethylene terephthalate clearly exhibits changes in the dielectric properties due to the immobilisation of dipoles during crystallisation; the reverse occurs during melting. The build-up and decay of interfacial polarisation during crystallisation and melting occurs in PET as well; the ohmic conductivity decreases however during isothermal crystallisation.

articleTitle: Influence of electrode materials on electrical conduction in polyphenylene sulphide in the high temperature region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Electrical conduction of PPS films has been investigated in the range of 100-160/spl deg/C. The results obtained manifests three characteristic dependence on the electric field. No dependence of electrical conduction on electrode materials was obtained in the low and medium electric field regions. The current increases with electric field superlinearly in the medium field region, and ionic hopping has been proposed as the dominant mechanism. The explicit dependence on electrode materials has been obtained in the high field region, where Au electrode gives larger current than Al electrode. That is, as the current shows the dependence on the positive electrode, hole injection is taken into account in the discussion of the conduction mechanism.

articleTitle: Charge storage of a new organic/inorganic hybrid film electret PVDF/SiO/sub 2/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A new method for manufacturing the organic/inorganic hybrid film electret PVDF/SiO/sub 2/ by the sol-gel process is presented. The process of preparing the hybrid films is described in detail. The influence of different process conditions on charge storage capability and charge stability for the hybrid film electret PVDF/SiO/sub 2/ were studied by means of constant voltage corona charging at room and elevated temperature, surface potential decay measurements and TSD spectra. The experimental results show that the hybrid film electret PVDF/SiO/sub 2/ has good storage capability.

articleTitle: Propagative cascading at the origin of very large cubic nonlinearities in quadratic polar molecular media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Very large nonlinear shifts ranging from /spl pi//4 to /spl pi//2 corresponding to n/sub 2/ as high as 10/sup -12/ cm/sup 2//W are observed in single crystal cored fibers of 4-(N,N-dimethylamino)-3-acetamidonitrobenzene (DAN). Self-phase modulation and direct interferometric measurements have unambiguously ascribed this behaviour to a cascading sequence of second harmonic generation followed by down frequency conversion.

articleTitle: Photoconductivity of poly((E,E)-[6.2]paracyclophane-1,5-diene) doped with low molecular weight acceptors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Poly((E,E)-[6.2]paracyclophane-1,5-diene) (PDE) exhibits high hole mobility due to a cofacial alignment of bridged aromatic rings, but it shows low photoconductivity. After sensitization with low molecular weight acceptors, the photoconductivity increases considerably. In a series of PDE doped with several benzoquinone derivatives it was found that with an increase of electron affinity of the dopant, the spectral sensitivity extends more into visible range. In the system showing the highest photoconductivity, PDE with 2,4,7-trinitrofluorenone, the maximum of the photoconductivity gain spectrum correlates with the charge-transfer absorption band. Strong field dependence of the photoconductivity gain is a consequence of field-dependences of both photogeneration and mobility.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents study of structural features of polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Molecular mobility at the glass-transition region of the block styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS) copolymers has been investigated by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC). The TSDC maxima, /spl alpha//sub 1/, have been attributed to the glass transition temperature of the butadiene phase T/sub /spl alpha//, B, according to differential thermal analysis data. The main features of the TSDC spectra are: 1) peak amplitude is a linear function of external field, 2) peak shape and its temperature position depend on the polarization temperature T/sub p/. Such results are meaningful for a dipole relaxation time distribution. The dipole distribution function of relaxation times has been calculated from the TSDC curve.

articleTitle: Polarization properties of layers in As-Se modified system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Charge processes which take place in chalcogenide glasses to a great extent determine the properties of these materials and therefore are decisive in their practical application. In this work we investigate the influence of an admixturing factor (Pb) on the polarization processes and on the transport of charge carriers in thin layers of chalcogenide glasses of As-Se system in an infralow frequencies region (10/sup -6/...10/sup -1/ Hz).

articleTitle: Surface charge decay characteristics for two-layer pure and iodine doped polystyrene system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The study has been made on 60 /spl mu/m thick solution grown single and two-layer pure and iodine (I/sub 2/) doped polystyrene (PS) specimens. For two-layer samples, I/sub 2/-doped layer was solution grown on previously obtained undoped layer on glass substrate. The samples were vacuum aluminized over central circular area of 3.6 cm diameter on one surface, and then were thermally polarized at different temperatures (T/sub p/) (i.e. 20, 75 and 100/spl deg/C) with 100 kV/cm polarizing field. Initial charge density has been found to be of 10/sup -8/ Coul/cm/sup 2/. The symbols (+) and (-) mean that positive and negative voltage were applied to the doped-layer side. For undoped and two-layer (+) the charge has always been found to be heterocharge. However, two-layer (-) are characterized with homocharge, when poled with high values of field and temperature.

articleTitle: On dielectric relaxation of glycine at high frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this work the dielectric relaxation time of glycine, a natural amino acid essential for normal development of the body has been reported. Using Q-meter method of measurement in the high frequency range of 10-30 MHz the real and imaginary components of the complex permittivity were computed. Using existing theories the dielectric relaxation times were obtained in the range of 6.92 n sec to 10.60 n sec when the sample of glycine in the powder form was subjected to pressures in the range of 5 to 8 tons. The result for dielectric relaxation times are in agreement with the theoretical computed values.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated currents in epoxy resin systems and epoxy resin/rubber blends
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The low temperature relaxation mechanisms of epoxy networks and blends were investigated by thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDG) techniques in the temperature range of 77 to 300 K. Two series of specimens, based on DGEBA cured with either TETA or DDM, were prepared. Specimens in the first series were mixed with different amounts of plasticizer thiocol. The influence of the absorbed water on the low temperature relaxations, and its plasticizing capability were studied, both affected by the presence of plasticizer and water in the specimens. In the second series, blends of CTBN with epoxy resin ER were prepared. Four dispersions are observed and ascribed to the CTBN phase, the ER phase and their interfaces.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated current study of crystalline benzene derivatives
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) and thermally stimulated polarization current (TSPC) of crystalline hexasubstituted halomethylbenzenes-pentachloronitrobenzene, pentachloroaniline, pentachlorotoluene, tetrachloro-m-xylene, pentabromotoluene, tetrachloro-o-benzene and bromopentamethylbenzene-was measured. The first five derivatives showed a TSDC peak and the corresponding TSPC peak, respectively obeying dipolar relaxation processes. However, the rest compounds showed a characteristic TSDC peak and the corresponding TSPC peak followed by more than one peak in the high temperature range of the main peak. The high temperature peaks are, presumably, due to benzene ring deformation induced by the mutual motion of plural adjacent methyl groups.

articleTitle: Interpretation of thermally stimulated depolarization currents using a modification of the coupling model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents are analyzed in the framework of Ngai's coupling model modified by introducing a continuous time-or temperature dependent change of the origin of time while keeping the parameters of the model constant in the whole temperature range. There is no need to define the glass transition temperature. The relaxation time at the compensation temperature can be calculated. Furthermore the analysis gives an explanation for the /spl alpha/-/spl beta/ bifurcation. The few available results are consistent with the scheme but there is a need for more experimental work to know how universal the formalism is.

articleTitle: The electret effect in poly-epoxypropylcarbazole
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The regularities of dark discharge in ionic contact mode and of thermoelectret effect as well as the plastifying influence of some solvents on these effects have been investigated for layers of poly-epoxypropylcarbazole (PEPCa) and of its complexes with trinitrofluorenone (TNF). Frequency-temperature dependences of dielectric spectra have been analysed for layers and for high-concentrated solutions of PEPCa in dioxane and methylene chloride, too.

articleTitle: Spontaneous electrical current in P(VDF/TrFE) copolymer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Short-circuit electrical currents were observed in 60:40 mol% P(VDF/TrFE) copolymers above 80/spl deg/C, temperature in which this polymer undergoes a structural ferro-to-paraelectric phase transition. The signal of this current was inverted when the sample is rotated so that the electrodes had their positions exchanged. Different combinations of metallic materials (aluminium, copper, nickel, and gold) were used as electrodes in metal(1)-polymer-metal(2) structures. Voltage signals were also detected in paraelectric samples, whose signal was equally dependent on the electrode combinations. This phenomenon is probably due to an electromotive force arising from different interfacial potential on both metal-sample interfaces.

articleTitle: Analytical aspects in the presence of polymeric materials in field gaps of HV insulation system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper a mathematical model should be found describing the behaviour of polymeric materials under high field stress. The model describes application of integral approach to numerical computation of fields in a multi-dielectric. The effect of varying both dielectric constant and dielectric thickness of the insulating material in field gaps on the electric field distribution have been investigated. In the present work, the study is on the estimation of nonuniform field in the presence of polymeric materials in the field gaps under different needle radius, gap distance. The effect of the ratio between dielectric length and plate electrode length (H/S) is also investigated.

articleTitle: Thermal-pulse investigation of poled nonlinear optical polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Poled nonlinear optical (NLO) polymer films are usually supported by substrates. This leaves two possibilities for investigating polarization and electric-field profiles in such samples with the thermal-pulse-technique: Thermal-pulse generation in the front electrode on the film or in the rear electrode between film and substrate. The influence of the substrate on the amplitude and on the long-time behavior of the thermal-pulse signal is theoretically treated. Experiments were performed on a poled double-layer sample consisting of a polymer film with NLO chromophores adhered to a similar polymer without chromophores, the latter film adhered to the substrate. The results demonstrate the validity of the proposed experimental approach.

articleTitle: Application of a rheological model to the simulation of ferroelectric hysteresis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A model of scalar hysteresis able in describing hysteretic behavior of ferro-electric materials is presented. It is one of the easiest examples of model of hysteresis with non-local memory and enjoys all mathematical properties of the classical Preisach one. Like all black box models (i.e. all models which have not relations to the physics of the phenomenon under description) it is necessary to define a procedure of identification of model's parameters. The discussion tries to outline a methodology to define a hysteresis model pointing out the problems related to the identification procedure.

articleTitle: Formation and destruction of polarization by migration of space charge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In a thermal electret of a polymer, excess charge, which is released from traps at high temperature, migrates in the polymer and forms a polarization under an applied electric field. We treat the density distribution of excess carriers by computer simulation calculation. Using a simple model of monoenergetic trap and monoenergetic transport states, we could explain the behavior of excess carriers in the process of polarization and depolarization. The calculations show that the excess charge gathers at the extreme end of a domain by the process of poling and that the accumulated charge hardly diminishes by the process of depolarization.

articleTitle: Relaxation processes in PVDF-BaTiO/sub 3/ composites revealed by TSP and TSD methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The electrical properties of PVDF-BaTiO/sub 3/ composites are studied experimentally. The TSP and TSD curves are compared and the conclusion is made that the decrease in conductivity is related to the buildup of the ferroelectric polarization. Importance of the thermal stimulation is stressed. The information on parameters of the relaxation processes is obtained by the RMA method. The experimental results are consistent with the model developed previously for the ferroelectric polymers.

articleTitle: Measurement of latent charge image using Pockels effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Highly sensitive optical measurement technique to visualize and quantity a latent surface charge image on a dielectric material has been developed by using Pockels effect and a computer image technique. This system has several improved performance, e.g., the sensitivity of 1 nC cm/sup -2/ and the spatial resolution of 200 /spl mu/m. In this paper, the basic measurement principle and the typical surface charge distribution of positive streamer produced by impulse high voltage (5 kV/sub peak/) are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of a VDF/TrFE copolymer-on-silicon pyroelectric sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a VDF/TrFE copolymer-on-silicon pyroelectric sensor. For an optimal design of a VDF/TrFE-on-silicon pyroelectric sensor, the one-dimensional diffusion equation is solved for the pyroelectric multilayer structure. The output current of the sensor is calculated. Improvement of the sensor can be obtained by: (a) etching the silicon substrate under the sensor element, and (b) an additional VDF/TrFE copolymer layer as thermal isolation. Different noise sources for a pyroelectric sensor have been calculated. The dielectric noise dominates the noise sources. This conclusion has been verified by measured values.

articleTitle: Modelisation of flexural and transverse vibrations of thin plates equipped with piezopolymer transducers. Application to sensors immersed in fluid and submarine fouling protection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The authors present a generalization of the S. Koshigoe and J.W. Murdock theoretical model. The considered structure vibrations are calculated and compared with experimental results. Complementary measurements of optical transmittance have been carried out by a spectroscopic study of glass plates immersed in a marine environment.

articleTitle: Effects of annealing on switching characteristics of VDF/TrFE copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Dynamical characteristics of the polarization reversal in vinylidene fluoride copolymers strongly depend on thermal and mechanical treatment. If a film quenched from melt is drawn and annealed above the Curie temperature T/sub c/, polarization reversal proceeds over several decades while it is completed within one decade if annealed below T/sub c/. X-ray measurement shows no significant difference in the crystalline structure among samples annealed at various temperatures, while SEM images reveal difference in the shape of lamellae among those samples. Dynamical properties are discussed in relation to the structure.

articleTitle: Application of new thermopiezoelectric effect to thermo- and piezoelectret records
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: It was originally shown that partially clamped piezoelectric crystals decrease the symmetry of their polarization response to thermal or elastic excitation. As a result any ordinary piezoelectric material (such as /spl alpha/-quartz) and even materials that are pyroelectric perpendicularly to their unique polar axis (such as Y-cut tourmaline) acquire the polar (vectorial) electric response on scalar thermal influence. In connection with this effect we discovered Y-surface thermoinduced electric charges on LiTaO/sub 3/ crystals which manifest themselves through electrooptical patterns. A "thermoelectret" effect is likely to be applied as reversible thermoinduced records. Our recent study uncovered a simple stress-induced method to produce well-defined and reversible records on Y-LiTaO/sub 3/ plates that can be ascribed to a "piezoelectret" nature.

articleTitle: Piezo- and pyroelectricity of BaTiO/sub 3//PMMA and PZT/PMMA composites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: In this paper, there are presented the investigations of the piezo- and pyroelectric properties for BaTiO/sub 3//PMMA and PZT/PMMA composites (0-3 connectivity). Samples of these materials have been obtained by polymerization of methyl methacrylate (MMA) where the fine particles of BaTiO/sub 3/ and PZT were dispersed. The piezoelectric constants (d, and g) ware measured by well-known static method, whereas the pyroelectric coefficient (p) by so-called quasi-static direct method. These parameters and, moreover, the figure of merit for piezoelectricity (d/sub h/g/sub h/) and pyroelectricity (p//spl epsi/') in dependence on volume fraction of the BaTiO/sub 3/ and PZT were determined.

articleTitle: Approximate calculation of the limiting flow line issued from a half emitting electrode inside a plane condenser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: An approximate calculation based on the Green's function method applied to the Laplace region bounded by the electrodes and a straight wall at a potential equal to the unperturbed space charge is performed in order to find the limiting flow line issuing from a half emitting electrode inside an infinite plane condenser. The results are compared with those provided by the enlarged Budd-Wheeler hodographic method previously obtained. An interesting and unexpected self-field effect was detected.

articleTitle: Optical poling of polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: We present an all-optical poling technique which permits the permanent polar ordering of organic chromophores embedded in polymer matrices. The microscopic processes involved, and their consequences on the dynamic and geometrical properties of this optical poling, are analyzed in the model. The authors use as an example azo-dye polymers.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Ultra thin polymer films fabricated with the self-assembly technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Ultra-thin films comprising alternating layers of polyacids, poly(styrene sulfonate) (PSS) or poly(vinyl sulfonic)-acids (PVS) and doped poly(o-methoxyaniline) (POMA) were produced using the self-assembly (SA) technique. The combination of POMA and polyacids is of particular interest, for the polyacid may prevent the POMA from undoping when the film is exposed to neutral or slightly basic solutions. Doped poly(o-alkoxyanilines) are suitable systems for SA because of their high solubility in water. The UV-visible absorbance spectra show a peak ranging from 585 nm to 800 nm depending on the doping level. The absorbance at the peak increases linearly with the number of deposited bi-layers, which indicates that equal amounts of material are adsorbed in each deposition procedure.

articleTitle: Optical investigation studies of corona and electron beam poled thin polymer films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The orientation of dipolar groups in thin polymer films induced by different poling methods can be observed by linear and nonlinear optical characterization. This concept includes the in-situ absorption studies of nonlinear optical polymers oriented by corona poling and the second harmonic generation (SHG)-measurement of thin fluoropolymer layers poled with the electron-beam technique.

articleTitle: Photoconducting polymers for photorefractive nonlinear optics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Photoconducting polymers doped with nonlinear optical molecules show important photorefractive properties. These new polymer composites are promising materials for photonic applications such as dynamic holographic storage and image processing. The photorefractive properties of a highly efficient polymer composite based on poly(N-vinylcarbazole) are investigated and discussed.

articleTitle: Photoassisted poling, at room temperature, of dye molecules in amorphous films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The photoisomerization of some anisotropic molecules modifies their orientational order and induces a macroscopic anisotropy which produces a dichroism and a birefringence. Starting from this well known property, we have demonstrated that the photoisomerization of some polar molecules, in the presence of a DC electric field, can induce the orientation of molecular dipoles, at room temperature, in materials for which this poling is possible only at high temperature (above T/sub g/), in the absence of optical pumping. This technique is promising for producing non centrosymmetric polymer (or sol-gel) films with second order optical nonlinearities patterned by photolithographic methods (for integrated optics: modulators, harmonic generation).

articleTitle: Electric properties of liquid crystalline polypeptide thin films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Linear poly(/spl gamma/-alkyl substituted-/spl alpha/, L-glutamate)s exhibit interesting thermal and morphological properties in the bulk state. We report on the electrical and thermal characterization of poly(/spl alpha/-alkyl substituted-/spl alpha/, L-glutamate)s using thermally stimulated polarization and thermally stimulated discharge current measurements as well as differential scanning calorimetry. The TSPC shows big variations at the onset of the melting during the heating of the sample and at the onset of solidification during cooling. In this region the activation energy can be very high. Values between 1.16 eV and 4.39 eV were obtained. For low fields the transition is not so well observed. In TSPC measurements some minimums appear at field reversal. The TSDC peak is very broad and moves to higher temperature as the polarization field or polarization temperature increases. The TSDC changes sign in some conditions, but this is not an intrinsic sample property.

articleTitle: Langmuir-Blodgett films from conjugated polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The recent developments on the main strategies for fabricating Langmuir-Blodgett (LB) films from conducting polymers are presented. Because this is a brief report, we concentrate on our latest results on films produced from parent polyaniline and poly(alkoxyanilines). It is found that the use of a pre-doped polymer on a subphase containing a doping agent enhanced significantly the quality of the Langmuir monolayer. When transferred onto a solid substrate the LB films are already in the doped state as confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy. LB films obtained with pre-doped poly(alkoxyanilines) exhibit electrochromism, with color changes from yellow to dark blue as the potential in an electrochemical cell is varied from -0.1 V to 0.7 V (versus SCE). In addition, good quality LB films were obtained with pre-doped, high molecular weight parent polyaniline.

articleTitle: Octupolar metal complexes for quadratic nonlinear optics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The classical molecular engineering schemes based on quasi one-dimensional dipolar charge transfer are enlarged to molecules with two- or three-dimensional contributions of octupolar origin. We report here a large increase in quadratic hyperpolarizability /spl beta/ values (up to 2.10/sup -27/ e.s.u.) of chiral ruthenium complexes upon successive complexation by one, two and three bipyridine derivatives. A strong metal-to-ligand charge transfer is evidenced from comparison of the experimental /spl beta/ value of the three-substituted complex with that deduced from a simple additive model of metal-ligand interaction.

articleTitle: Electrode material effect on TSDC and I-V characteristics of polypropylene films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Measurements of TSDC and studies of Current-Voltage characteristics have been carried out on polypropylene films using various deposits of materials as electrode layers. The results obtained with layers of SiC, SiN, SiO/sub 2/, GeC, C have been compared. An interesting application of this study may be the improvement of power capacitor performances.

articleTitle: Photothermal dielectric spectroscopy: A novel technique for the determination of the dielectric, pyroelectric and thermal properties of thin dielectric films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A novel technique is described which combines dielectric measurements with a time and frequency dependent photothermal excitation. The sample, a thin metallized film, is placed in an aluminium ring which serves as a heat sink. At different temperatures both the dielectric and pyroelectric spectra are obtained by applying sequentially an AC-voltage and a modulated heat flux to the sample. The thermal properties are assessed by the application of a local laser heating; the resulting increase in the mean sample temperature is recorded by high precision capacitance measurements at a fixed frequency. From the equilibrium increment /spl Delta/C(T) and the temperature dependence of the capacitance C(T) we can find the temperature increment /spl Delta/T(T) and thus the thermal conductivity, while from the transient response /spl Delta/C(T,t) the thermal diffusivity can be obtained. Combination of all information further yields the pyroelectric coefficient and the specific heat. Experiments on PVDF were performed at temperatures from -60 to 110/spl deg/C to show the capabilities of the new method.

articleTitle: Electrode effect on carrier injection in polyvinyl pyrrolidone: polymethyl methacrylate polyblend films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Mechanism of charge production and its persistent in polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP), polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and their polyblend films have been analysed using short circuit thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) technique as a function of electrode metal with constant polarizing field (3.5/spl times/10/sup 4/ volts/cm) and polarizing temperature (70/spl deg/C). The TSDC spectra of PMMA consist of a sharp peak around 155-170/spl deg/C, for Al-Ag/Cu systems, however. The TSDC spectra of PVP and polyblend films have been found to be characterized with two peaks located around 90-100/spl deg/C and 140-160/spl deg/C along with an additional current maxima which has been found around 205/spl plusmn/50/spl deg/ C in a direction which is opposite to both the peaks. The observed polarization is explained in terms of existence of hetero charge due to dipole orientation and detrapping of charges injected from the electrodes with subsequent space-charge formation.

articleTitle: Water related electronic traps at the surface of silicon nitride electret layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: A novel technique for measuring the value of charge and for evaluating its centroid position in the electret layers is proposed. A scanning mercury probe is employed for measurements of flat band voltage shift and erasure current of a semiconductor-electret structure placed in environments with high humidity. We used this technique for photoconductivity measurements in silicon nitride films. For the first time deep electronic water related traps in silicon nitride were observed.

articleTitle: Preparation and characterization of polyimide and optically non-linear transparent polyimide: ceramic films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Transparent polyimide films (PI) were prepared and their dielectric and optical properties were studied. The PI films show almost 80% transmission in the 600 nm to 1600 nm wavelength range. The dielectric constant was found to be about 3.5 and it does not vary significantly upto 160/spl deg/C. Transparent PI:BaTiO/sub 3/ and PI:LiNbO/sub 3/ films were prepared by in situ polymerization of PI and gelation of BaTiO/sub 3/ and LiNbO/sub 3/ sols respectively. The X-ray diffractograms clearly indicate the formation of BaTiO/sub 3/ and LiNbO/sub 3/ in these films. The dielectric constant of PI:BaTiO/sub 3/ films was found to be 10 and its variation with temperature shows a Curie peak at about 120/spl deg/C. The dielectric constant of PI:LiNbO/sub 3/ films was found to be about 6. The loss is very small in these films. In PI:LiNbO/sub 3/ films, optical phase conjugation using degenerate four wave mixing technique has been observed and the experimental results are given. It is concluded on the basis of the results that these films may find useful applications in non linear optical devices.

articleTitle: TSD currents in some rare-earth-oxide-based thin-film sandwiches
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: Characteristics of thermally stimulated currents in metal/insulator/metal (MIM) thin-film sandwiches based on some rare earth oxides (sesquioxides of ytterbium, dysprosium and holmium) are presented. Electrical measurements were carried out for temperatures from 297 K to 500 K. The influence of the polarizing temperature, voltage and heating rate on the TSD characteristics was examined. The TSD thermograms for examined different rare earth oxides were very similar and are characterized by a single peak connected with 0.5-0.7 eV traps.

articleTitle: Polarization phenomena associated with the microstructure of PEEK
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 8th International Symposium on Electrets (ISE 8)
abstract: The microstructure of Poly (Ether Ether Ketone)/PEEK has been analysed by Thermo Stimulated Currents/TSC. The amorphous phase has been characterized by the kinetic of the molecular mobility involved in dielectric relaxation. Around the glass transition temperature, a complex TSC peak is observed: The lower temperature component, situated at 150/spl deg/C, has been associated with cooperative movements in the "mobile amorphous phase" of PEEK. The higher temperature component, situated at 162/spl deg/C, has been attributed to the existence of a "rigid amorphous phase" with local order induced by crystallites. The evolution of mechanical properties of PEEK upon crystallinity can be explained with the hypothesis of a three phase model: crystalline phase, mobile amorphous phase and rigid amorphous phase.
